item.title: “Get Julian Sayin Out of Columbus”: Fans React as OSU QB’s Interception Puts Buckeyes in Trouble vs Indiana
item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin (10) runs during the first half of the NCAA football game against the Texas Longhorns at Ohio Stadium on Aug. 30, 2025. Credit: Imagn Last season, the Indiana Hoosiers snapped Ohio State’s winning streak, and as the two teams meet for the first time since, Julian Sayin and company have a chance to renew their matchup. However, in the second quarter, Sayin tried to pass to Jeremiah Smith, but Amare Ferrell intercepted it, which eventually led to an Indiana touchdown. Soon enough, Ohio State fans took to social media and slammed Sayin, with many calling out the quarterback. “Get Julian Sayin out of Columbus, man,” said one Ohio State fan. After intercepting Julian Sayin, Amare Ferrell had a 23-yard return for Indiana. This eventually led to a 7-yard rushing touchdown from Turbo Richard, giving the Hoosiers the lead with 13:54 remaining in the second quarter. A few minutes later, Sayin had another chance to connect with Jeremiah Smith, who actually beat the double coverage this time. The catch was still contested, with the quarterback missing the throw. This forced Ohio State to try to score another field goal, but the team failed. Nick Saban Says To Stop Jeremiah Smith, Indiana Must Stop Julian Sayin So far, Jeremiah Smith has been the favorite to win the Heisman this year, and this is all thanks to him playing well with quarterback Julian Sayin. Ahead of the game, on “College GameDay,” former Alabama coach and ESPN analyst Nick Saban said that to stop Jeremiah Smith, one must stop Julian Sayin. “I think the best way to slow down Jeremiah Smith is to affect the quarterback, and that’s the one thing Ohio State’s going to have to do today: They’re going to have to handle Indiana’s pressure,” Saban said. “Julian Sayin has been affected by pressure. His completion percentage goes down to 56%. Indiana has 49 tackles for loss, so they’re good at getting you behind the sticks, and they have 20 sacks, which is among the top in the country.” With seven national championships, Nick Saban knows a thing or two about stopping an opponent’s star player, and so far, Indiana has been handling Julian Sayin. item.title: 44 Years Later, Steven Spielberg's Scariest Movie of All Time Is Officially Back on Streaming
item.description: Poltergeist , which is currently available to stream on HBO Max, follows an ordinary suburban family who begin to experience strange things in their home. Furniture and toys move on their own, a glass of milk shatters out of nowhere, and the youngest child in the family, five-year-old Carol Anne (Heather O'Rourke), begins to communicate with beings through the television. At first these events are dismissed, but during a thunderstorm one night, a tree outside the windows of the kids’ room crashes in and snatches the boy. Then, a portal opens in their closet, sucking Carol Anne into another dimension. With help from some paranormal investigators, the family tries everything to bring her back.

item.title: Why Alex de Minaur’s Grand Slam dream may be further away than ever after latest statistic emerges
item.description: Alex de Minaur is one of the most likeable players on the ATP Tour, and he makes it so easy to root for him. After all, he boasts a work ethic that demands admiration, and an upbeat personality that continues to win fans. However, for all his effort and application, at the Grand Slam level, it feels as though he remains wanting. The Australian is a seven-time major quarter-finalist, having never made it further than that stage. As impressive as he can be at these events, the barrier is clear. And, what’s even more worrying is a recent statistic that has emerged, which makes his Grand Slam dream only feel further away. Alex de Minaur’s worrying record against the best players on the ATP Tour Realistically, if Alex de Minaur is to break past his current quarter-final hoodoo, or even go all the way, he will likely have to defeat one of Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner, Novak Djokovic or Alexander Zverev. However, his record against all four makes for rather dire reading, especially when excluding team events like the ATP Cup, United Cup, and the Davis Cup. If those results are removed, the 27-year-old has never beaten any of this elite quartet, losing all 29 meetings. His aspiration for the majors is clear, and De Minaur has not been shy in voicing it either. Viewing a statistic as damning as this does make it hard to imagine him ever surpassing that quarter-final block, especially given his inability to capitalise at this year’s Roland Garros or Wimbledon events, where Alcaraz was absent from both, and Sinner and Djokovic both lost early in Paris. Despite his dire combined record, De Minaur retains his patented positivity, even if it has felt like more and more negativity has been creeping into some of his post-match assessments. What Alex de Minaur said about challenging Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz last year After his loss at Roland Garros, De Minaur gave an emotional interview , where he said: “It kind of feels like the door has been shut in front of me. Once in a blue moon you get an opportunity like this, and you have to be able to take it, and I did exactly the opposite today.” It marked a sad day for normally such an upbeat player, as he realised the gravity of his failure. Opportunities like that do not come around often, as, before this year, Alcaraz and Sinner had shared all of the last eight Grand Slam titles. However, it did mark a pretty sharp change from De Minaur’s comments after the ATP Finals at the back end of 2025. There, he almost issued a war cry, insisting he was getting closer to competing with the world’s best. He argued: ”I feel like I’ve gained a lot of momentum recently in these types of matches [against Sinner and Alcaraz]. Photo by Neal Simpson/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images “I’ve gone from a stage where, hey, you go out there, you compete, but you’re not really getting a lot of chances. item.title: 5 Bold Predictions For NY Giants Week 6 Matchup Versus The New Orleans Saints
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The (3-1-1) New York Giants will look to remain undefeated at home this season as they take on the (1-4) New Orleans Saints on Sunday at MetLife Stadium. With their 27-27 tie to the Washington Commanders last Sunday, the Giants are at least a game and a half ahead of every team in the NFC East. But head coach John Harbaugh knows his team cannot afford a setback against the struggling Saints. This matchup should be one of the most exciting games of Week 6. Let’s dive into some bold predictions for Big Blue versus New Orleans. Malik Nabers Will Have Over 150 Receiving Yards Oct 11, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers (1) catches a touchdown pass as Washington Commanders cornerback Mike Sainristil (0) defends at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images If there were any doubts about whether Malik Nabers was fully recovered from his two knee surgeries, he erased them with his performance against the Washington Commanders. He caught 11 passes for 121 yards and a touchdown. He and Jameis Winston are steadily building a rapport, which has resulted in explosive plays over the last two games. This week they’ll face a New Orleans defense that has yet to allow a wide receiver to have 100 yards this season. Nabers will put an end to that as he will torch their secondary and have over 150 receiving yards. Tyrone Tracy Jr. Will Have Over 100 All-Purpose Yards Oct 11, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. (29) runs the ball during the third quarter against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images With the addition of rookie right guard Francis Mauigoa, many felt New York would have one of the best ground games in the league. But through five games, they’re averaging 109 yards per game, and their longest run of the year was 22 yards by Jaxson Dart in Week 1. None of the team’s running backs are averaging over 3.6 yards per carry. To make matters worse, Cam Skattebo has fumbled four times. After falling out of favor with Harbaugh in the preseason due to his fumbles and failed blitz pickups, Tyrone Tracy Jr. could be poised to see an increase in his workload. Tracy is the team’s most elusive back but has just seven carries for 22 yards for the season. In hopes of giving his ground game a spark, expect Harbaugh to turn to the 26-year-old running back to showcase his ability as a runner and receiver. This will result in his first big game of 2026, as he will have over 100 all-purpose yards. Mandatory Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images With the addition of rookie right guard Francis Mauigoa, many felt New York would have one of the best ground games in the league. But through five games, they’re averaging 109 yards per game, and their longest run of the year was 22 yards by Jaxson Dart in Week 1. None of the team’s running backs are averaging over 3.6 yards per carry. To make matters worse, Cam Skattebo has fumbled four times. After falling out of favor with Harbaugh in the preseason due to his fumbles and failed blitz pickups, Tyrone Tracy Jr. could be poised to see an increase in his workload. Tracy is the team’s most elusive back but has just seven carries for 22 yards for the season. In hopes of giving his ground game a spark, expect Harbaugh to turn to the 26-year-old running back to showcase his ability as a runner and receiver. This will result in his first big game of 2026, as he will have over 100 all-purpose yards. The Defense Will Sack Tyler Shough 6 Times Oct 11, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; New York Giants linebacker Abdul Carter (3) sacks Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) during the first quarter at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Big Blue’s pass rush has finally come to life over the last two games. After only recording one sack in the first three weeks, they have seven sacks in the last two. The Saints have the 29th-ranked rushing offense in the league, so they are going to rely on their passing game with second-year quarterback Tyler Shough . Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson is aware of this and will unleash his front seven on Shough. New York pass rush will overwhelm the Saints’ offensive line and have their best performance to date as they will sack Shough six times. J.J. McCarthy Will Come In For 10 Plays New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) is shown on the sideline, Sunday, October 4, 2026, in East Rutherford. J.J. McCarthy entered the game for five snaps in Week 5, ran the ball twice for two yards, and did not attempt a pass. It was his first game action as a member of the Giants, and Harbaugh indicated they’ll continue to have packages for McCarthy. Look for the team to ramp up the 23-year-old quarterback’s activity this week. As a result, McCarthy will come in for 10 plays and attempt his first pass with the team. He could see even more action if Winston struggles. The Offense Will Not Commit A Turnover Oct 11, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (44) fumbles the ball during overtime against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images One of the team’s biggest issues is that they turn the ball over too frequently. They’ve committed at least one turnover in four of their five games, including five turnovers in the last two weeks. If New York keeps being turnover-prone, it’s going to come back and bite them, as the Saints have five takeaways on the year. But on Sunday, the Giants play mistake-free football and will not commit a turnover.

item.title: “Julian Sayin Allergic to Throwing to Jeremiah Smith”: Fans React as Indiana Shuts Down OSU WR in 1H with “Calvin Johnson” Coverage
item.description: Wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. © IMAGN Indiana appeared to use extra coverage while facing Ohio State star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith on Saturday. Known for his explosive plays, Smith is not getting an easy one-on-one matchup against the national champions. Analyst Pat McAfee noted similarities between how Smith was defended and how Calvin Johnson was defended back in the day. Johnson, nicknamed “Megatron,” was one of the NFL’s most physically imposing receivers. Smith has drawn similar comparisons after two Indiana defenders appeared to be near him. “We’re getting REAL close to the Calvin Johnson punt gunner coverage for Jeremiah Smith,” McAfee wrote. Fans shared their reactions to Indiana’s strategy to stop Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin from getting easy access to one of the best wide receivers in college. “Sayin allergic to throwing to Jeremiah Smith,” one fan wrote. “No other WR gets covered like this in college football,” one fan noted. “Stop insulting Calvin’s dominance. Jeremiah Smith isn’t that,” one fan remarked. “Always a legend,” one fan wrote. “No joke, Pat, at this point I don’t think press with two over him in addition is off the table. Use 3,” one fan said. “Jeremiah Smith gets the Shaq treatment. They simply won’t call PI by smaller DB,” one fan compared the receiver to an NBA legend. Indiana Gets Concerning Jeremiah Smith Prediction Ahead of Ohio State Showdown Jeremiah Smith is easily one of the best receivers in college football this season. The Ohio State Buckeyes receiver entered Saturday’s game with 916 receiving yards and 11 touchdowns in six games this season. Despite Indiana’s unbeaten 6-0 start this season, NBC analyst Todd Blackledge believes the Hoosiers won’t be able to stop Smith on the field. “Another issue where I think, and this will show itself, you know, how they’re going to deal with Jeremiah Smith, they’re not as good in the boundary corner as they were last year with D’Angelo Ponds,” Blackledge said. “I mean, they felt like he could really, they could count on him to do what he needed to do, lock something down, they could be creative and cover each other places with their simulated pressures and all of that.” So far in the first two quarters, Indiana’s strategy might be working because Sayin hasn’t thrown a lot to Smith in the first half despite Ohio State trailing 7-3 at the end of the second quarter. He has two receptions for 20 yards. item.title: Angel Reese reveals her immediate plan after Dream’s WNBA Finals Game 1 loss to Valkyries
item.description: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images Angel Reese reveals her immediate plan after Dream’s WNBA Finals Game 1 loss to Valkyries appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Game 1 of the WNBA Finals was highly competitive, but the Golden State Valkyries emerged victorious over the Atlanta Dream with a 68-64 win. Gabby Williams led the way for Golden State with 26 points, while Allisha Gray — who was questionable to play before being made available — had 19 points for Atlanta. Meanwhile, Angel Reese turned in a strong 14-point, 12-rebound double-double. After the game, Reese revealed what she is planning on doing following the defeat, via Winsidr. “Yeah, just going back into the film room and figuring out things that we messed up on, things that we can be better at,” Reese told reporters. Reese had a quiet second half following a big first half. When asked about that after the game, Reese said she simply wasn’t aggressive enough from an offensive standpoint, via ClutchPoints. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I don’t think they (Valkyries) really did anything (to slow her down in the second half). Maybe that was just on me,” Reese said. “I wasn’t aggressive enough with the ball… So, definitely going to do a better job of that next game.” The Dream still kept things competitive on the road. They are certainly still in the series. Bouncing back as soon as possible will be of the utmost importance, of course. It goes without saying, but avoiding an 0-2 deficit is the goal. Game 2 of the WNBA Finals between the Dream and Valkyries is scheduled for Monday night at 8 PM ET in San Francisco as Angel Reese will look to lead Atlanta to a crucial win on the road. Related: 1 brutal stat that proves why Dream lost Game 1 to Valkyries Related: Allisha Gray questionable for Game 1 vs. Valkyries, deemed game-time decision

item.title: Tennessee defeats Alabama for third straight time at Neyland Stadium
item.description: No. 14 Tennessee (6-1, 3-1 SEC) defeated No. 7 Alabama (5-2, 3-2 SEC), 26-10, on Saturday in Week 7. The Vols won their third consecutive game against Alabama at Neyland Stadium. Tennessee sophomore quarterback George MacIntyre made his second career start. He completed 21-of-31 passing attempts for 197 yards and one interception. DeSean Bishop led the Vols in rushing yards (159). He also scored two rushing touchdowns on 32 attempts. Wide receiver Mike Matthews led Tennessee with seven receptions and 85 receiving yards. The Vols totaled 347 yards (197 passing, 150 rushing). Tennessee forced four Alabama turnovers. Amare Campbell was the Vols' leader for tackles (eight), while Tyree Weathersby and Jeremiah Telander recorded two sacks each. Tennessee kicker Cooper Ranvier converted 4-of-4 field goal attempts. The Vols were also 5-for-5 in red zone opportunities. Alabama totaled 201 yards (147 passing, 54 rushing). Follow Vols Wire on Facebook and X (formerly Twitter). This article originally appeared on Vols Wire: Tennessee defeats Alabama for third straight time at Neyland Stadium

item.title: Dodgers fan favorite acknowledges potential final season with LA in message: ‘If this is it for us’
item.description: Kiké Hernandez may have played his final game with the Dodgers. The fan favorite acknowledged the uncertain future he faces as he enters free agency in an Instagram post in which Hernandez expressed his gratefulness for fans. Los Angeles Dodgers’ Kike Hernandez gestures toward his dugout after hitting a two-run home run during the seventh inning of a baseball game against the Cincinnati Reds, Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026, in Los Angeles. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill “LA, we fell short of our big goal. But looking at the big picture, what a ride these last three years were!!” Hernandez wrote in the Instagram caption. “If this is it for us…. Once again, I will always be thankful for you guys & I will forever love ya! #JustAKidFromPR,” Hernandez said. President of baseball operations Andrew Friedman brought Hernandez back on a one-year deal last offseason, saying the “door was always open” for the utilityman. It remains unclear whether that will be the case this winter as Hernandez hits free agency again. Hernandez has built his career as an electric personality in the Dodgers’ dugout and a clutch bat every October. His postseason numbers are simply mystifying with Hernandez coming to life every fall. Kike Hernandez #8 of the Los Angeles Dodgers in the dugout during the game against the Colorado Rockies Getty Images But as the Dodgers look to get younger, the front office may go in another direction this offseason. The Dodgers assembled the most expensive roster in baseball, which also happened to be the oldest. While the Dodgers won 100 regular-season games with their veteran core, the back-to-back World Series champions were swept by a hungrier, younger Brewers team. Hernandez, who has been a key part of Los Angeles’ back-to-back World Series titles, could play another major role in the postseason. Getty Images The four-game sweep in the National League Championship Series may alter the Dodgers’ plans as the front office attempts to build another winning roster. Only time will tell whether Hernandez is a part of that group.

item.title: Lots to like in Providence basketball's exhibition win over Pittsburgh
item.description: PROVIDENCE – Exhibition or not, Saturday’s effort at Amica Mutual Pavilion will offer some encouragement for Providence men’s basketball fans. The Friars never trailed Pittsburgh while making easy work of an old Big East rival, pulling away over the final 12 minutes for what was ultimately a comfortable victory. Miles Byrd led four players in double figures, and Providence dished out 22 assists, a number it bettered only once during a lost 2025-26 campaign. The Friars started fresh with this 87-64 dismissal of the Panthers, and the 4,601 fans in attendance got a first glimpse of what will be the 100th team in program history. “Exhibition game, but proud of the effort,” Providence coach Bryan Hodgson said. “That’s really what’s important – getting better week by week and then coming out here and playing with the right attitude and effort.” Providence played a closed scrimmage with Boston College last weekend and was without Devin Vanterpool (left ankle) and Ryan Sabol (left shoulder) in this one. Those absences didn’t stop the Friars from mounting the deciding 21-2 run midway through the second half. Jonathan Powell’s 3-pointer that made it a 57-52 game was the last field goal Pittsburgh made to draw within two possessions. “It’s fun getting up and down,” Byrd said. “Every hooper would love to play this type of way.” Here are three takeaways from the first public viewing of the Friars in this 2026-27 campaign. New emphasis on assists Providence willingly shared the ball throughout, assisting on 66.7% of its 33 made field goals. item.content:encoded: PROVIDENCE – Exhibition or not, Saturday’s effort at Amica Mutual Pavilion will offer some encouragement for Providence men’s basketball fans. The Friars never trailed Pittsburgh while making easy work of an old Big East rival, pulling away over the final 12 minutes for what was ultimately a comfortable victory. Miles Byrd led four players in double figures, and Providence dished out 22 assists, a number it bettered only once during a lost 2025-26 campaign. The Friars started fresh with this 87-64 dismissal of the Panthers, and the 4,601 fans in attendance got a first glimpse of what will be the 100th team in program history. “Exhibition game, but proud of the effort,” Providence coach Bryan Hodgson said. “That’s really what’s important – getting better week by week and then coming out here and playing with the right attitude and effort.” Providence played a closed scrimmage with Boston College last weekend and was without Devin Vanterpool (left ankle) and Ryan Sabol (left shoulder) in this one. Those absences didn’t stop the Friars from mounting the deciding 21-2 run midway through the second half. Jonathan Powell’s 3-pointer that made it a 57-52 game was the last field goal Pittsburgh made to draw within two possessions. “It’s fun getting up and down,” Byrd said. “Every hooper would love to play this type of way.” Here are three takeaways from the first public viewing of the Friars in this 2026-27 campaign. New emphasis on assists Providence willingly shared the ball throughout, assisting on 66.7% of its 33 made field goals. Malik Mack and Gavin Hightower closed with seven apiece while serving as the primary ballhandlers. “We trust each other to make shots,” Mack said. “We’re an unselfish basketball team that wants to move the ball and go from a good shot to a great shot.” That’s some carryover for Hodgson from his South Florida team last season. The Bulls were a top-50 team nationally, according to KenPom.com, assisting on 58.4% of made baskets. The Friars were the opposite – 294th nationally at just 47.5%, their lowest number since a final season under Keno Davis in 2010-11. “We have a very unselfish group,” Hodgson said. “We built the roster that way. They trust one another.” Willingness to shoot from deep Arrinten Page and Ryan Mela flashed some shooting touch they hadn’t necessarily shown previously in their careers. Page closed 4-for-8 from 3-point range and Mela finished 3-for-4 from deep. That marksmanship helped lift Providence to a 15-for-39 effort as a team – they attempted just 31 2-point shots and eight free throws on the day. Page is a 6-foot-11 big man who attempted just 16 3-pointers with USC in 2023-24 and nine with Cincinnati in 2024-25. He shot more frequently from deep with Northwestern last year, closing 11-for-44. Page had never made four 3-pointers in any two-game stretch, let alone in a single contest. “Not that it’s a focus, but he can do that at a high level,” Hodgson said. “That’s why we recruited him. We’re going to play a little differently than where he was at before us.” Mela nearly doubled his attempts last year, going from 30 3-pointers taken as a freshman to 58 as a sophomore. He could eclipse that second number as a junior playing in a system that encourages shots from deep. Hodgson’s three teams at Arkansas State and South Florida were all top-100 groups nationally in terms of 3-pointers taken versus overall field goal attempts. Status report on injuries The Friars used all 10 available scholarship players in this one. Vanterpool was in a walking boot and using a scooter to make his way around the floor. He was projected as a scoring guard after a transfer from Florida Atlantic and the first captain named by Hodgson midway through preseason camp. Vanterpool suffered his injury during practice this week. “I can’t tell you when he’ll be back – it's nothing crazy or serious,” Hodgson said. “But this is the time of the year where you can make sure he gets the full rest that he needs on that ankle to make sure that he’s ready to go when we tip the ball for real.” Sabol was in street clothes at the end of the bench along with his fellow guard. He was hurt in practice after getting caught in ball screen action and spraining his left shoulder joint. The transfer from Buffalo is also considered day-to-day, and his status for next weekend’s exhibition against Georgia Tech is uncertain. “Maintenance things right now,” Hodgson said. “Ryan is also day-to-day.” PITTSBURGH (64): Jonathan Powell 3-10 7-8 15, Chase Foster 4-9 0-0 8, Baye Ndongo 6-8 0-0 13, Jalil Bethea 1-6 3-4 5, Naithan George 3-4 2-2 9, A’lahn Sumler 4-9 2-3 12, Armani Mighty 0-0 2-3 2, Macari Moore 0-0 0-1 0, Dominique Diomande 0-0 0-0 0, Ibrahim Souare 0-0 0-0 0, Jermal Jones 0-1 0-0 0. Totals 21-49 16-21 64. PROVIDENCE (87): Javon Bardwell 3-7 0-1 6, Samson Aletan 0-0 0-0 0, Ryan Mela 5-7 2-2 15, Miles Byrd 5-16 3-4 17, Malik Mack 4-10 1-1 10, Arrinten Page 6-10 0-0 16, Gavin Hightower 3-9 0-0 7, Clyde Walters 1-2 0-0 2, Jacob Bannarbie 3-3 0-0 6, Leonardo Marangon 3-6 0-0 8. Totals 33-70 6-8 87. Halftime – Pro., 37-28. 3-point FG – Pitt. 6-21 (Powell 2-7, Foster 0-2, Ndongo 1-1, Bethea 0-5, George 1-1, Sumler 2-5), Pro. 15-39 (Bardwell 0-1, Mela 3-4, Byrd 4-12, Mack 1-4, Page 4-8, Hightower 1-4, Walters 0-1, Marangon 2-5). Rebounds – Pitt. 26 (Ndongo 7), Pro. 42 (Byrd 7). Assists – Pitt. 14 (Sumler 5), Pro. 22 (Mack 7, Hightower 7). Turnovers – Pitt. 16 (Ndongo 6), Pro. 13 (Bardwell 4). Attendance – 4,601. bkoch@providencejournal.com On X: @BillKoch25 This article originally appeared on The Providence Journal: Lots to like in Providence basketball's exhibition win over Pittsburgh

item.title: Penn State’s Losing Streak Extends to Four Games in Michigan Loss
item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Tony Siracusa, CFB Managing Editor Penn State’s losing streak has grown to four games with the 21-18 loss to Michigan on Saturday afternoon. The Nittany Lions held a 3-0 lead at halftime, but multiple turnovers and a quarterback change by the Wolverines flipped the second half in Michigan’s favor. Chase Sowell had the game of his five-year career, catching 11 passes for 151 yards and a touchdown. His receptions and yards are both career highs. But it wasn’t enough for Penn State to get the win. Penn State’s Losing Streak Extends to Four Games Penn State Takes the Early Lead Penn State’s offense has struggled to find rhythm all season, and it continued to be an issue all day, except the opening drive. The Nittany Lions drove 69 yards in a stunning 16 plays, but ended with just a 24-yard field goal. It was the longest drive of the season for the blue and white, burning 9:02 off the clock. Quarterback Rocco Becht got hot quick, completing 7-of-8 attempts for 40 yards. His favorite targets were Sowell (three catches for 21 yards) and Andrew Rappleyea (three catches for 10 yards). Michigan’s opening drive was less eventful, moving 32 yards in nine plays. Defensive end Caleb Bacon made a big tackle for loss on freshman running back Savion Hiter to force a punt at Penn State’s 35-yard line. Lots, and Lots of Punts There were six combined punts in the second frame. The first came when Sowell entered the injury tent after suffering an apparent ankle injury on his 13-yard reception. Three plays later, Penn State folded and Michigan took over at its 26-yard line. However, the Wolverines went 3-and-out as the boos began to rain down in the Big House. Sowell returned to action and Becht dotted a fade perfectly over Sowell’s shoulder for a 26-yard gain. The drive stalled again, but Penn State got the ball back after a circus interception where Jamison Patton broke up Andrew Marsh’s catch, causing the ball to pop up into the hands of a trailing Zion Tracy. POPPED UP FOR A PICK! https://t.co/GCQ3JUPGh3 — CBS Sports (@CBSSports) October 17, 2026 The following drive, again, didn’t amount to much. Penn State ran six plays for just 15 yards. Michigan’s possession was another eyesore, going for a loss of two yards in three plays. Penn State took over on its own 21 with 1:51 remaining before halftime, still up 3-0. Becht found Sowell for the sixth time of the half for 14 yards, then again for a 27-yard gain, but it was called back for offensive pass interference, and the drive quickly ended. Michigan was driving from its own 32-yard line with 1:07 left. The Wolverines went 32 yards in three plays until Bryce Underwood was intercepted for a second time. This one was an insane one-handed grab by freshman corner Josiah Zayas to take the Nittany Lions’ 3-0 lead into the half. The Nittany Lions held a 3-0 lead at halftime, but multiple turnovers and a quarterback change by the Wolverines flipped the second half in Michigan’s favor. Chase Sowell had the game of his five-year career, catching 11 passes for 151 yards and a touchdown. His receptions and yards are both career highs. But it wasn’t enough for Penn State to get the win. Penn State’s Losing Streak Extends to Four Games Penn State Takes the Early Lead Penn State’s offense has struggled to find rhythm all season, and it continued to be an issue all day, except the opening drive. The Nittany Lions drove 69 yards in a stunning 16 plays, but ended with just a 24-yard field goal. It was the longest drive of the season for the blue and white, burning 9:02 off the clock. Quarterback Rocco Becht got hot quick, completing 7-of-8 attempts for 40 yards. His favorite targets were Sowell (three catches for 21 yards) and Andrew Rappleyea (three catches for 10 yards). Michigan’s opening drive was less eventful, moving 32 yards in nine plays. Defensive end Caleb Bacon made a big tackle for loss on freshman running back Savion Hiter to force a punt at Penn State’s 35-yard line. Lots, and Lots of Punts There were six combined punts in the second frame. The first came when Sowell entered the injury tent after suffering an apparent ankle injury on his 13-yard reception. Three plays later, Penn State folded and Michigan took over at its 26-yard line. However, the Wolverines went 3-and-out as the boos began to rain down in the Big House. Sowell returned to action and Becht dotted a fade perfectly over Sowell’s shoulder for a 26-yard gain. The drive stalled again, but Penn State got the ball back after a circus interception where Jamison Patton broke up Andrew Marsh’s catch, causing the ball to pop up into the hands of a trailing Zion Tracy. POPPED UP FOR A PICK! https://t.co/GCQ3JUPGh3 — CBS Sports (@CBSSports) October 17, 2026 The following drive, again, didn’t amount to much. Penn State ran six plays for just 15 yards. Michigan’s possession was another eyesore, going for a loss of two yards in three plays. Penn State took over on its own 21 with 1:51 remaining before halftime, still up 3-0. Becht found Sowell for the sixth time of the half for 14 yards, then again for a 27-yard gain, but it was called back for offensive pass interference, and the drive quickly ended. Michigan was driving from its own 32-yard line with 1:07 left. The Wolverines went 32 yards in three plays until Bryce Underwood was intercepted for a second time. This one was an insane one-handed grab by freshman corner Josiah Zayas to take the Nittany Lions’ 3-0 lead into the half. OH BABY WHAT A PICK! https://t.co/VBzyCTWYeC — CBS Sports (@CBSSports) October 17, 2026 Michigan Changes QBs Michigan opened the second half with four-star freshman quarterback Tommy Carr leading the offense onto the field. He completed his first pass over the middle to JJ Buchanan for 11 yards, but couldn’t pick up another first down. The Wolverines subsequently punted for a fourth time. However, it all went downhill for Penn State when Becht’s first pass of the half was picked off by Rod Moore on a diving grab. Carr took a shot downfield on an unsuccessful flea-flicker, but the Wolverines hit big with a 43-yard touchdown run up the middle from Bryson Kuzdzal . Penn State, now down 7-3, was able to get Sowell the ball twice for 33 yards, but Becht threw his second pick of the second half at the Michigan 26. Michigan’s offense came alive after a dormant first half. Carr hit Hogan Hansen for 22 yards, then Hiter rushed for 18 more. Jordan Marshall picked up a fourth-and-2, and Carr rushed 23 yards to set up Marshall’s 1-yard touchdown. Photo courtesy: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Mistakes, Mistakes, Mistakes Penn State, now down 14-3, sent Becht out with the offense after his two previous turnovers. He hit Sowell twice for 21 yards, and found Gabe Burkle for a 20-yard gain to enter the red zone. Then, Carson Hansen plowed forward for a 2-yard touchdown, and Becht found Ben Brahmer on a shovel pass for the 2-point conversion. With the lead cut to 14-11, Michigan looked to get some cushion, but went 3-and-out and gave Penn State the ball with 10 minutes left in regulation. But the Nittany Lions shared the same fate. Hiter sparked the Wolverines with a 41-yard burst on the first play of the drive, but Penn State’s defense responded by stopping Michigan’s offense on the next three plays. With six minutes remaining, the Nittany Lions drove 17 yards in two plays, but Becht was strip-sacked for his third turnover of the game, and the Wolverines took over at the Penn State 13-yard line. Michigan ran four plays before Carr’s 12-yard touchdown sealed the Nittany Lions’ fate. Becht got Sowell a 24-yard touchdown before time expired. The Last Word This was one ugly loss for Penn State. The long opening drive felt as if the offense would finally put it all together, but it all unravelled quickly. Becht’s three turnovers were brutal. Michigan scored all 21 points off his mistakes, and they were all in the second half. The only thing he did well was get Sowell the ball. Becht finished with 267 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions, a fumble, and completed 28-of-44 pass attempts. While this loss is mostly on Becht’s second-half collapse, Penn State still didn’t show any improvement in two key areas . The run game averaged 2.2 yards per carry for a second consecutive game . Hansen was the leading rusher with 51 yards on 15 carries and a touchdown. Penn State’s pass rush got home once, and it was Rojas again. He got the lone sack in Penn State’s loss to USC last week. Credit to the rest of the defense, though. Rojas went off again with 12 tackles, two for a loss and a sack. Zayas and Tracy had impressive interceptions. The run defense is still concerning, allowing 221 yards and all three touchdowns. Main Image: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images

item.title: Dynamite Beatdown: Daniel Dubois Takes Out Fabio Wardley in Rematch
item.description: What To Know Daniel Dubois staked his claim as the world’s top heavyweight with a destructive performance in London on Saturday In the first defense of his WBO World Heavyweight title, Dubois stopped Wardley in two rounds. Did Wardley come back too fast after his loss to Dubois five months ago? Daniel Dubois threw a massive stick of dynamite into the ring from the opening bell, landing a massive right hand to Fabio Wardley’s jaw just 17 seconds into their rematch on Saturday. It was the first knockdown in Wardley’s professional career. Referee Steve Gray could have stopped the fight there. Wardley’s trainer, Ben Davison, could have stopped the fight there. But Wardley was allowed to continue. Five minutes later, Davison stepped in to stop the damage being done to Wardley. Just like that, the much-anticipated rematch was over at 2:21 of round two. Dubois of London (24-3, 23 KOs) successfully defended his WBO World Heavyweight title over Wardley of Ipswich, England (20-2-1, 19 KOs). “Shout out to the whole team for the effort, man. Fabio is a great warrior coming in for a second time, but it was my time, in my era. I have to rule right now,” said Dubois with a rarely seen grin on his face. Daniel Dubois Slams the Door From the first right hook, Fabio Wardley never had a chance. item.content:encoded: What To Know Daniel Dubois staked his claim as the world’s top heavyweight with a destructive performance in London on Saturday In the first defense of his WBO World Heavyweight title, Dubois stopped Wardley in two rounds. Did Wardley come back too fast after his loss to Dubois five months ago? Daniel Dubois threw a massive stick of dynamite into the ring from the opening bell, landing a massive right hand to Fabio Wardley’s jaw just 17 seconds into their rematch on Saturday. It was the first knockdown in Wardley’s professional career. Referee Steve Gray could have stopped the fight there. Wardley’s trainer, Ben Davison, could have stopped the fight there. But Wardley was allowed to continue. Five minutes later, Davison stepped in to stop the damage being done to Wardley. Just like that, the much-anticipated rematch was over at 2:21 of round two. Dubois of London (24-3, 23 KOs) successfully defended his WBO World Heavyweight title over Wardley of Ipswich, England (20-2-1, 19 KOs). “Shout out to the whole team for the effort, man. Fabio is a great warrior coming in for a second time, but it was my time, in my era. I have to rule right now,” said Dubois with a rarely seen grin on his face. Daniel Dubois Slams the Door From the first right hook, Fabio Wardley never had a chance. Photo: Queensberry Promotions Both Wardley and Dubois vowed to deliver another epic battle after their 2026 Fight of the Year candidate, a high bar. Oddsmakers favored Dubois, giving Wardley a chance only if he could strike early as he did in the first fight, and make it stick. Dubois never gave him a chance. Credit to Wardley for surviving the initial knockdown which would have dropped a rhino, and the next five minutes of the fight. Outside a boxing ring, Dubois would be charged with aggravated assault. Wardley’s trainer Ben Davison admitted a few days after the first fight that he made a mistake not stepping in earlier. He was on the top step near the end of the first round with the towel in his hand, but Wardley got out of the first round. Referee Steve Gray had nerves of steel in not stopping the fight himself at any point in the first round. Wardley didn’t have enough time in the corner to recover. The damage left from the first fight emerged as the second round ticked by. Finally, Davison did the right thing and the towel came into the ring. Dubois: “I Had Bad Intentions” Daniel Dubois came in focused with only one outcome in mind: a more significant victory than in the first fight. Photo: Queensberry Promotions “I had bad intentions from the beginning, and this is God’s victory tonight, and we done we done well,” said Dubois. “This time, we just had to go out there and show that we mean business, and that’s what we did tonight.” Wardley: “The Game Is The Game” Wardley made no excuses for the outcome in the rematch, but vowed it wasn’t the end. “Look, it’s never fun to lose, but it is what it is. The game is the game. I’ve always thrown myself in with the best competitors out there, with the best in the business, the toughest, the biggest, hardest, meanest guys around. So, look, there’s no shame in the loss when you’re putting yourself in and testing yourself against the best. “Daniel’s a testament to coming up short and coming again, and I’ll be looking to do the exact same thing,” said Wardley. Too Much Too Soon For Fabio Wardley? Was it too soon for Fabio Wardley to take the rematch? Hindsight is 20-20. Photo: Queensberry Promotions The analysis immediately turned to whether Wardley rushed the rematch after taking tremendous punishment from Dubois in the first fight. Wardley disagreed. “Not at all. Look, I just came in. I didn’t execute the game plan properly tonight. That was all. I hold my hands up to that. It’s entirely down to me,” explained Wardley. Wardley also absolved his team, including head trainer Ben Davison, who’s now seen two of his three heavyweight stars, Dubois and Moses Itauma, take losses. “When I step through the ropes, it’s only myself. It’s only me and me bouncing around in the ring and doing everything. There’s no blame to be passed around. When I win, it’s all me as well. So, look, we’ll go back to the drawing board as a team. There’s no shame in losing to a great competitor like Daniel.” The Heavyweight Division Outlook It will be wise for Wardley to sit out for a longer spell, reassess and put in some months in the gym in 2027 before coming back. Queensberry Promotions and Frank Warren will welcome him with open arms. Wardley is likeable, popular, and easy to work with. In the meantime, Warren said he would be working toward unification fights in 2027. “I’ve got to say, Fabio Wardley, what a brave guy! I mean, his heart is unbelievable. But it was Daniel’s night. It was a superb performance, a powerful performance. “And next year we’re going to see some more great fights, some big fights, and Fabio will come back as well,” said Warren. Filip Hrgovic Stokes the Fire IBF World Heavyweight champion Filip Hrgovic took in the action with Frank Warren of Queensberry Promotions. Photo: Queensberry Promotions Before Dubois left the ring, Warren invited newly minted IBF World Heavyweight champion Filip Hrgovic up for a chat. The smiling Croatian wasted no time getting there and offering his thoughts. “ Look, it was easy night for Daniel. He did a good job, quick, quick win. So he’s ready to fight me in March, right?” laughed Hrgovic. Dubois was all about it. “I want to have a rematch with him. I want to get that belt. I want to get my old belt back and yeah, rule the division.” Hrgovic has long wanted to bring a heavyweight fight to his native Croatia. Queensberry is likely to stage a title defense for Hrgovic in Croatia against Frank Sanchez, and then the chatter will begin about a Dubois vs Hrgovic showdown. With Agit Kabayel vs Nelson Hysa ticket sales now well over 42,000, let’s see if Croatia’s enthusiasm catch match it. When the heavyweight division is healthy and competitive, it’s good for all of boxing. Here’s to a great year ahead in boxing in 2027. Dubois Wardley 2 Undercard Notes The undercard served as a domestic showcase for British prospects. It’s a positive development that keeps fighters busy, but it doesn’t always make for riveting entertainment. The co-main event left everyone unsatisfied as announcer Thomas Treiber announced a majority draw between Louie O’Doherty of Essex (12-0-1, 3 KOs) and Michael Gomez Jr. of Manchester (23-2-1, 8 KOs). Scores were 115-114 for Gomez, and 114-114 on the other two cards. Gomez Jr. had appeared to pull out the win and was visibly upset. O’Doherty retains his British and Commonwealth lightweight title. A rematch is highly likely. Among the few undercard highlights was the second round KO by Irish heavyweight prospect Adam Olaniyan. Photo: Queensberry Promotions Promising Irish heavyweight Adam Olaniyan of Tallaght (5-0, 5 KOs) got back into the ring six weeks after scoring a first-round knockout on the Katie Taylor undercard at Croke Park. Olaniyan took two rounds for a TKO win over Dan Garber of Yorkshire (14-10, 2 KOs). Olaniyan is 20 years old and a work in progress. He has the looks and charisma to take him far if his skills keep pace. “What a crowd, what an atmosphere. I couldn’t have asked better for my fifth professional fight,” said Olaniyan. Heavyweight Bakhodir Jalolov of Uzbekistan (18-0, 15 KOs) ground out a decision win behind a fifth-round knockdown over Solomon Dacres of London (10-2, 3 KOs). Scores were 99-91, 99-91, and 99-90. Jalolov was never remotely threatened. Jalolov seems more interested in seeking a third gold medal at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games. It would be an impressive accomplishment, but he’s not going to get a lot of opportunities as a heavyweight if he walks through dull fights. Highly regarded super bantamweight amateur Manny Safari won his pro debut by stopping journeyman Jake Pollard of London (1-122-1). Yes, that’s right. P

item.title: Bears Add RB as Kyle Monangai Replacement Ahead of Falcons Game
item.description: Running back Kyle Monangai of the Chicago Bears. Getty Chicago Bears reveal bad Kyle Monangai injury news amid latest D'Andre Swift update Getty NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 22: Zavier Scott #36 of the Minnesota Vikings runs the ball during the first half of the NFL Preseason 2025 game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on August 22, 2025 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) Getty The Chicago Bears made a handful of significant roster moves one day ahead of their Week 6 showdown with the Atlanta Falcons, including adding running back Zavier Scott to the active roster to fill in for the absent Kyle Monangai. Courtney Cronin of ESPN reported all of the Bears’ roster moves on Saturday, October 17 via an X post. “The Bears made room on the 53 for Kyler Gordon by putting Dayo Odeyingbo on IR, a move that Ben Johnson felt they would be able to avoid earlier in the week. Safety Xavier Woods was also released,” she wrote. “DB Nick McCloud was signed to the 53 from the PS. LB Buddy Johnson and RB Zavier Scott were elevated from the PS to game day roster.” Bears Struggled Mightily to Run Football Against Packers After Injuries to Kyle Monangai, D’Andre Swift Getty Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai. Chicago’s run game struggled without Monangai against the Green Bay Packers last weekend like it has not all season, amassing just 81 yards and one score on 24 carries . Monangai suffered a turf toe injury during a career-game against the New York Jets in Week 4 that has now sidelined him for a second consecutive contest. D’Andre Swift also exited early in the second half last weekend against the Packers due to hip and knee issues, though he is a full-go in Atlanta on Sunday. The Bears elevated Scott to the active roster for Week 5, though he did not log any carries. However, he did play nine snaps on the special teams unit. Third-string RB Roschon Johnson logged five carries for just six yards against Green Bay, second only to Swift’s nine hauls. Wide receiver Luther Burden III ran the football four times, though to just two total yards of success. Zavier Scott May Get First Carries as Bears RB Against Falcons Getty Running back Zavier Scott of the Minnesota Vikings . Scott is an explosive runner and chose the Bears during the offseason after the Minnesota Vikings cut him in late August with the intention of bringing the 27 year old back to the practice squad in early September. LB Buddy Johnson and RB Zavier Scott were elevated from the PS to game day roster.” Bears Struggled Mightily to Run Football Against Packers After Injuries to Kyle Monangai, D’Andre Swift Getty Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai. Chicago’s run game struggled without Monangai against the Green Bay Packers last weekend like it has not all season, amassing just 81 yards and one score on 24 carries . Monangai suffered a turf toe injury during a career-game against the New York Jets in Week 4 that has now sidelined him for a second consecutive contest. The Bears elevated Scott to the active roster for Week 5, though he did not log any carries. However, he did play nine snaps on the special teams unit. Third-string RB Roschon Johnson logged five carries for just six yards against Green Bay, second only to Swift’s nine hauls. Wide receiver Luther Burden III ran the football four times, though to just two total yards of success. Zavier Scott May Get First Carries as Bears RB Against Falcons Getty Running back Zavier Scott of the Minnesota Vikings . Scott is an explosive runner and chose the Bears during the offseason after the Minnesota Vikings cut him in late August with the intention of bringing the 27 year old back to the practice squad in early September. He presumably made that choice because he believed he would have a stronger chance at earning the RB3 spot behind Swift and Monangai this year than achieving the same positional security in Minnesota after the Vikings drafted RB Demond Claiborne in the sixth-round back in April. Scott got 32 carries last year in Minnesota, tallying 114 rushing yards . He also caught 14 passes for 98 yards and one score. Chicago schemed up six run plays for wide receivers in Green Bay, including the aforementioned four for Burden as well as one each for rookie Zavion Thomas and Kalif Raymond. Part of that strategy may have involved the team’s inability to rush the football effectively in a traditional manner due to injury concerns and because the Bears fell so far behind and kept making things worse by turning the ball over five times on the afternoon. If Chicago can get things back on track against the Falcons with a healthy Swift in the RB1 role, the absence of Monangai and the ineffectiveness of Johnson and the WR group rushing the football against the Packers should open up a few opportunities for Scott to show what he can offer the Bears’ offense. item.title: Kiké Hernandez sends touching message to Dodgers fans amid uncertain free agent future
item.description: Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Kiké Hernandez sends touching message to Dodgers fans amid uncertain free agent future appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the Los Angeles Dodgers were swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS, the team now moves on to the offseason, where there are decisions to be made about which players to bring back. With the Dodgers’ future of Kiké Hernandez uncertain, the utility player himself posted a message to social media about his situation. Taking to his Instagram account, Hernandez said that Los Angeles missed out on winning their third World Series title, still saying how much of a “ride” it’s been the past three years. Pondering if this will be the end of his career with the franchise, he expresses gratitude to the fans. “LA; we fell short of our big goal,” Hernandez wrote, via Dodgers Nation. “But looking at the big picture, what a ride these last three years were!! If this is it for us…. Once again, I will always be thankful for you guys & I will forever love ya! #JustAKidFromPR” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Kiké Hernández acknowledges his time with the Dodgers could be coming to an end in a thank you message to the fanbase on his Instagram: “LA; we fell short of our big goal. But looking at the big picture, what a ride these last three years were!! If this is it for us…. Once… pic.twitter.com/iC3UDkNZn8 — Dodgers Nation (@DodgersNation) October 17, 2026 Kiké Hernandez wants to return to the Dodgers Hernandez has now played 10 seasons with the Dodgers, as his one-year deal has just now run its course with the team eliminated from the playoffs. Entering the offseason as a free agent, his top desire is to return to the team, and if not, he wants to play for a “winning team,” per Fox Sports. “Every time I look at my career, I kind of obviously go back to this place. I’ve been here the longest. I hope I get back,” Hernandez said in the clubhouse. “I feel like I have a lot left this year. I thought it was gonna be a good year for me on the personal side.” “I thought that once my surgery healed, I’d finally be healthy and able to play,” Hernandez continued. “And then, of course, s*** happened. But yeah, I would love to be back. I would love to have one more try, trying to win another one. I don’t really know what’s gonna happen. I hope I’m back.” "I feel like I have a lot left… I would love to be back." – Kiké Hernández on his future with the Dodgers pic.twitter.com/crpRNmA1zO — FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 16, 2026 Dealing with injury this season, Hernandez has played in 41 games this season, with the 35-year-old player hoping to improve in 2027. Related: Analyst drops extremely bold Shohei Ohtani prediction for 2027 season with Dodgers Related: John Smoltz says quiet part out loud about Brewers embarrassing Dodgers in NLCS

item.title: Oilers Getting Much-Needed Boost as Key Names Return
item.description: EDMONTON, CANADA - APRIL 16: Connor McDavid #97, Zach Hyman #18 and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins #93 of the Edmonton Oilers celebrate a second-period goal during the game against the Vancouver Canucks at Rogers Place on April 16, 2026, in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. (Photo by Leila Devlin/Getty Images) Getty The Edmonton Oilers appear poised to get some relief in their battle against injuries, with three key contributors set to return to the lineup for Saturday’s rematch against the Utah Mammoth. Based on Saturday’s morning skate lines and head coach Mike Babcock’s comments, Zach Hyman, Colton Dach, and Jake Walman will all slot back in. The trio is ready to rock 👊 #LetsGoOilers pic.twitter.com/xn1CZJDBPf — Edmonton Oilers (@EdmontonOilers) October 17, 2026 This is huge for the Oilers, who have been doing their best to stay afloat with so many bodies out. Essentially, they’ve been missing their entire second line for five games and depth guys were being asked to punch well above their weight class. They were doing an admirable job, losing only one game in regulation this season. Still, it was a lot to ask. Now, with three regular contributors back, the Oilers have some depth again. What Does the Oilers Lineup Look Like Now? The top line stays untouched, with Vasily Podkolzin still flanking Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl. This line has been dominant, but Babcock admitted he was overusing them. That’s where the real impact shows up. Dach and Hyman join Kasperi Kapanen on the second line, a significant boost for a group that’s been without both forwards for a stretch. It then moves names like Alex Formenton, Owen Michaels, and Mathieu Joseph down to the third line, where they fit much better. Filip Hallander, Trent Frederic, and Isaac Howard round out the fourth line. The depth will be a welcome change. Babcock said after the team’s first regulation loss on Thursday that his top guys’ minutes were out of control. “I look at it every night and go, ‘What the heck am I doing?’” Babcock said, adding, “I’m also trying to survive right now.” Are Some Oilers Losing Their Spots? Josh Samanski and Max Jones slide into extra roles as a result, which could signal their futures. Given the number of injuries, nothing is set in stone, but both have arguably been put into the lineup as extras just to fill holes. On the back end, Walman returns to the third pairing alongside Ty Emberson, pushing Shakir Mukhamadullin into the seventh-defenseman spot rather than a regular shift. In net, Tristan Jarry is expected to get the start, looking to build on his recent form after a shaky start to the year. Both Jarry and Devon Levi have steadied themselves in recent appearances, giving Babcock at least one area of consistency to lean on while the rest of his lineup works its way back to full health. If these three returning players can stay in the lineup, it could mark a turning point for an Oilers team that’s been waiting for reinforcements. Soon enough, they’ll get Ryan Nugent-Hop

item.title: 49ers Announce Nick Bosa Decision Ahead of Commanders Game
item.description: San Francisco 49ers DE Nick Bosa is expected to miss a decent chunk of time with a calf injury Getty San Francisco 49ers edge rusher Nick Bosa. Getty Nick Bosa of the San Francisco 49ers is coming off his second ACL injury Getty The San Francisco 49ers held a team practice on Saturday. They have an extra day to prepare for their game against the Washington Commanders. The Week 6 matchup is scheduled for Monday, Oct. 19, with kickoff at 5:15 p.m. PST. The 49ers enter the NFC showdown with a 5-0 record (3-0 NFC West) after their thrilling win against the Seattle Seahawks. The Commanders hold a 1-3-1 record. They tied the New York Giants 27-27 during Week 5. Nick Bosa’s Status Against the Commanders 49ers star DL Nick Bosa’s status remains unlikely after the 5-time Pro Bowler missed Saturday’s practice. Update: 49ers ruled OUT Nick Bosa for Monday’s game against the Commanders. #49ers Nick Bosa is officially OUT for MNF against the Commanders, per Kyle Shanahan pic.twitter.com/oA3bkQWr5D — OurSF49ers (@OurSf49ers) October 17, 2026 The 49ers hoped to get Bosa back for their Monday night game against the Commanders. Bosa has been sidelined for the past three games after suffering a calf injury during practice before their Week 3 matchup against the Miami Dolphins . However, the 5-time Pro Bowler did not practice again on Saturday. Matt Barrows of The Athletic reported which 49ers players did and did not practice. “ Romello Height (illness), Gracen Halton (quad) & James Thompson (ankle) on hand for the start of practice, but no Nick Bosa,” Barrows wrote on X. Romello Height (illness), Gracen Halton (quad) & James Thompson (ankle) on hand for the start of practice, but no Nick Bosa. It's looking like his return will be Week 7, barring a setback. It also appears Mike Evans will not practice at all this week w/ rib/Achilles issues. — Matt Barrows (@mattbarrows) October 17, 2026 “It’s looking like his return will be Week 7, barring a setback. It also appears Mike Evans will not practice at all this week w/ rib/Achilles issues,” Barrows added about Bosa and Evans. Bosa has not practiced all week leading up to Monday’s game. It continues to trend towards Bosa being unlikely to play against the Commanders. Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area shared his thoughts on whether Bosa would play on Monday. The 49ers hit the practice field in about an hour. At this point, I think Kyle Juszczyk and Mike Evans will play Monday night against Washington, and Nick Bosa will not. — Matt Maiocco (@MaioccoNBCS) October 17, 2026 “The 49ers hit the practice field in about an hour. Getty Nick Bosa of the San Francisco 49ers is coming off his second ACL injury Getty The San Francisco 49ers held a team practice on Saturday. They have an extra day to prepare for their game against the Washington Commanders. The Week 6 matchup is scheduled for Monday, Oct. 19, with kickoff at 5:15 p.m. PST. The 49ers enter the NFC showdown with a 5-0 record (3-0 NFC West) after their thrilling win against the Seattle Seahawks. The Commanders hold a 1-3-1 record. They tied the New York Giants 27-27 during Week 5. Nick Bosa’s Status Against the Commanders 49ers star DL Nick Bosa’s status remains unlikely after the 5-time Pro Bowler missed Saturday’s practice. Update: 49ers ruled OUT Nick Bosa for Monday’s game against the Commanders. #49ers Nick Bosa is officially OUT for MNF against the Commanders, per Kyle Shanahan pic.twitter.com/oA3bkQWr5D — OurSF49ers (@OurSf49ers) October 17, 2026 The 49ers hoped to get Bosa back for their Monday night game against the Commanders. Bosa has been sidelined for the past three games after suffering a calf injury during practice before their Week 3 matchup against the Miami Dolphins . However, the 5-time Pro Bowler did not practice again on Saturday. Matt Barrows of The Athletic reported which 49ers players did and did not practice. “ Romello Height (illness), Gracen Halton (quad) & James Thompson (ankle) on hand for the start of practice, but no Nick Bosa,” Barrows wrote on X. Romello Height (illness), Gracen Halton (quad) & James Thompson (ankle) on hand for the start of practice, but no Nick Bosa. It's looking like his return will be Week 7, barring a setback. It also appears Mike Evans will not practice at all this week w/ rib/Achilles issues. — Matt Barrows (@mattbarrows) October 17, 2026 “It’s looking like his return will be Week 7, barring a setback. It also appears Mike Evans will not practice at all this week w/ rib/Achilles issues,” Barrows added about Bosa and Evans. Bosa has not practiced all week leading up to Monday’s game. It continues to trend towards Bosa being unlikely to play against the Commanders. Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area shared his thoughts on whether Bosa would play on Monday. The 49ers hit the practice field in about an hour. At this point, I think Kyle Juszczyk and Mike Evans will play Monday night against Washington, and Nick Bosa will not. — Matt Maiocco (@MaioccoNBCS) October 17, 2026 “The 49ers hit the practice field in about an hour. At this point, I think Kyle Juszczyk and Mike Evans will play Monday night against Washington, and Nick Bosa will not,” Maiocco wrote on X. Getty San Francisco 49ers edge rusher Nick Bosa. 49ers Defensive Line Steps Up Without Nick Bosa The 49ers have received meaningful contributions across their defensive line despite Bosa’s absence. In San Francisco’s win over Seattle, the 49ers recorded 5 sacks from 5 different players and 7 tackles for loss. Notably, rookie DL Gracen Halton stood out. He recorded 3 tackles, 2 tackles for loss, 1 sack, 1 forced fumble and a fumble recovery for a touchdown. Defensive linemen Keion White , Sebastian Valdez and Osa Odighizuwa each recorded a sack on QB Sam Darnold . Getty Nick Bosa of the San Francisco 49ers is coming off his second ACL injury Nick Bosa’s Injury Struggles Continue Bosa returned in time for the 49ers’ regular-season opener against the Los Angeles Rams after suffering a torn ACL in Week 3 of the 2025 season. He looked like the disruptive pass rusher that 49er fans have witnessed throughout his 8-year NFL career. Ultimately, after playing just three games last season and two so far this year, durability remains Bosa’s biggest hurdle. The edge rusher has recorded 7 tackles, 2 tackles for loss and a QB hit through the first two games this season. item.title: Instant reactions to Alabama's ugly road loss vs. Tennessee
item.description: On Saturday afternoon, the Alabama Crimson Tide traveled for the latest chapter of the Third Saturday in October at Neyland Stadium, a venue that has given the program fits in recent trips . One of the SEC's most storied rivalries, it was eventually more of the same for Alabama on Saturday afternoon. The Crimson Tide were plagued by a slow start offensively, and went on to struggle mightily in a number of different areas. As a result, Alabama suffered yet another road loss to Tennessee in a game where they never led , 26-10. A game that simply did not feature a lot of positives for the Crimson Tide, let's take a look at some instant reactions to Alabama's latest loss in Neyland Stadium. Alabama has ugly offensive showing To keep it simple, this was likely one of the worst offensive showings we have seen from Alabama in recent memory. The Crimson Tide could not get anything going at any point during the game, finishing with only 201 yards of total offense. Alabama also committed four turnovers, and struggled mightily on third down by going 2-of-13, as well as 1-of-3 on fourth down. The Crimson Tide also had only seven first downs the entire game. Alabama's rough start in first half While the offense struggled the entire game, Alabama really put themselves in a hole early with a rough showing in the first half. At halftime, Alabama trailed 12-10 following an offensive half that included only 93 total yards, three turnovers, and a combined 0-of-8 on third-and-fourth downs. Alabama loses the line of scrimmage A major storyline coming in, Alabama lost the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball Saturday afternoon. The Crimson Tide offensive line gave up five sacks to only one for Alabama's defense, while the Volunteers also out-rushed Alabama in all, 150-54, headlined by a lengthy drive in the fourth quarter that essentially iced the game for Tennessee. Alabama loses back-to-back games As a result of Saturday's road loss at Tennessee, Alabama has now dropped back-to-back games for the first time since 2013. This is also Alabama's third consecutive loss to Tennessee in Neyland Stadium after defeats in both 2022 and 2024. Contact/Follow us @RollTideWire on X, and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Alabama news, notes and opinion . This article originally appeared on Roll Tide Wire: Instant reactions to Alabama's ugly road loss vs. Tennessee

item.title: Big Cleveland sports day: Browns, Guardians to play back-to-back on Sunday
item.description: Every year, there is a reminder that there is nothing like baseball playoffs (except hockey playoffs, maybe. Full disclosure: hockey and soccer are not my sports, but I do respect them). The NFL playoffs, especially when our Cleveland Browns are in them, are amazing, but there is something different about every pitch mattering for a three-, five-, or seven-game series. With the Cleveland Guardians squaring off with the Tampa Bay Rays, Browns CB Denzel Ward’s involvement (along with many other Cleveland sports names like Cavaliers star Donovan Mitchell ) has been fun to see. Of course, Ward now owning part of the Guardians is a piece of his connection with the team. Sunday will be a big sports day in Cleveland. After the Guards were rained out on Friday night, Game 5 versus the Rays will be held Sunday at 5 PM. Perhaps Ward will join fans who attend the Browns Week 6 matchup with the Baltimore Ravens at 1 PM by hightailing up to Progressive Field (still The Jake to many of us) as quickly as possible for Game 5. The Guardians currently have a 2-1 lead in the ALCS with Game 4’s first pitch at 8 PM on Saturday night. Could you imagine if the Browns knock off the hated Ravens around 4:05 PM and then the Guardians’ first pitch less than an hour later is for a chance to go to the World Series on Sunday?! A big sports day in Cleveland. Anyone got tickets to go to both games? If not, are you planning to watch the Guardians Game 5 of the ALCS after the Browns Week 6 contest? Join the conversation! item.title: Ohio State’s Jeremiah Smith Makes It Personal With Indiana After Revenge Win
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA - OCTOBER 17: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes celebrates a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA - OCTOBER 17: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes celebrates a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty The Ohio State Buckeyes had revenge on their minds entering Saturday’s showdown against the Indiana Hoosiers. Following a hard-fought 19-15 victory, superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith made it clear that last year’s painful loss was still fresh in the team’s memory. Ohio State entered the highly anticipated Big Ten matchup looking to settle unfinished business against Indiana. The Hoosiers defeated the Buckeyes on Dec. 6, 2025, in the Big Ten championship game, giving Ohio State plenty of motivation heading into their latest meeting. Following Saturday’s victory, Smith spoke with Fox Sports about the importance of beating Indiana and the patience required throughout the afternoon. While the star receiver expressed satisfaction with his performance, his comments about last year’s defeat revealed just how personal this matchup had become. Jeremiah Smith Reveals Ohio State’s Revenge Motivation Against Indiana Smith was asked during the Fox Sports postgame broadcast about remaining patient while waiting for opportunities to make an impact. “Yeah, just staying patient. That’s what my coaches and teammates told me all game,” Smith said. “Just be patient. It’s going to come, and eventually it came. I’m happy I made a play today.” The talented receiver understood that opportunities would eventually arrive, even against an Indiana defense determined to limit Ohio State’s explosive offense. However, Smith’s most revealing comments came when the conversation shifted toward last year’s defeat and whether the Buckeyes carried additional motivation into Saturday. “Yeah, definitely, man,” Smith said. “We remember what happened Dec. 6 last year. They beat us, and we knew we had to come out here and be focused and win a game. That’s all that mattered today.” Those comments tell an important story about Ohio State’s mindset. The Buckeyes weren’t simply preparing for another ranked opponent. They were preparing for a program that had already beaten them on one of college football’s biggest stages. And judging by Smith’s response, that memory hadn’t faded. Ohio State Gets Its Revenge, but Indiana Makes Buckeyes Earn It Ohio State’s revenge victory didn’t come easily. The Buckeyes struggled to consistently move the football against Indiana’s defense, while quarterback Julian Sayin’s injury created additional uncertainty for the offense. That’s what my coaches and teammates told me all game,” Smith said. “Just be patient. It’s going to come, and eventually it came. I’m happy I made a play today.” The talented receiver understood that opportunities would eventually arrive, even against an Indiana defense determined to limit Ohio State’s explosive offense. However, Smith’s most revealing comments came when the conversation shifted toward last year’s defeat and whether the Buckeyes carried additional motivation into Saturday. “Yeah, definitely, man,” Smith said. “We remember what happened Dec. 6 last year. They beat us, and we knew we had to come out here and be focused and win a game. That’s all that mattered today.” Those comments tell an important story about Ohio State’s mindset. The Buckeyes weren’t simply preparing for another ranked opponent. They were preparing for a program that had already beaten them on one of college football’s biggest stages. And judging by Smith’s response, that memory hadn’t faded. Ohio State Gets Its Revenge, but Indiana Makes Buckeyes Earn It Ohio State’s revenge victory didn’t come easily. The Buckeyes struggled to consistently move the football against Indiana’s defense, while quarterback Julian Sayin’s injury created additional uncertainty for the offense. Indiana had opportunities to steal the victory late, including a potential game-winning touchdown attempt on its final possession. However, the Hoosiers couldn’t complete the comeback, allowing Ohio State to escape with a four-point victory. For Smith, the final score was ultimately what mattered most. His comments reflected a team that understood the significance of the matchup long before kickoff. Indiana’s previous victory provided motivation, but Ohio State still needed to execute when the opportunity arrived. Getty BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA – OCTOBER 17: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes celebrates a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) The win also carried implications beyond personal satisfaction. Ohio State strengthened its position in the Big Ten race while proving it could survive a difficult road test against elite competition. There are still legitimate concerns surrounding the Buckeyes’ offensive consistency and Sayin’s health moving forward. Nevertheless, those questions shouldn’t overshadow the significance of defeating a team that had previously gotten the better of them. Smith didn’t need to deliver an elaborate speech or disrespect Indiana to explain what Saturday meant. He simply pointed to one date: Dec. 6. For Ohio State, that was apparently all the motivation it needed. item.title: NFL predictions: Which running game excels in Browns-Ravens matchup to take over the AFC North?
item.description: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (3-2) take on the Baltimore Ravens (4-1). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. Can the Browns’ Run Defense Come Through? I’ve harped on this a bunch of times already, but last week’s game was mostly a non-factor for what I think of the Browns, except for one thing (I’ll get to that in a bit) due to the weather conditions. The weather is set to be great in Cleveland for Sunday’s big divisional game against the Ravens. If you jump forward to the predictions this week, though, I’m picking the Ravens, even with knowing Tyler Huntley is starting for them. I certainly think the Browns can win, and am only putting the edge slightly in Baltimore’s favor, but the big reason centers around Cleveland’s run defense and the status of Mason Graham and Mike Hall. The Ravens rank 3rd in the NFL in rushing yards per game (164.4) and are also 3rd in yards per carry (5.07). Side note: It seems pretty stunning that with how poor the Browns’ rushing attack has been, they are ranked 21st in rushing yards per game . The Browns’ run defense is 18th in rushing yards allowed per game (117.4) and 23rd in rushing yards per play allowed (4.48). They allowed their first rushing touchdown of the season last week against a Jets rushing attack that had previously been anemic. For a team that has relied on close, last-second victories, I see that successful rushing attack for the Ravens being the defining factor this week in them taking over the game late. High Stakes for Cleveland The stakes couldn’t be higher for Cleveland this week. If they win, they go back into first place in the AFC North, and would have victories over two division rivals already. If they lose, they are suddenly two games back of first place, and without the tiebreaker, which really makes it like three games back. Here are some of the positives I can think of this week, along with some general notes: I liked what Isaiah Bond did in training camp, and it’s unfortunate that his time to shine came in rainy conditions, which likely contributed to a couple big dropped passes. With that said, KC Concepcion was meant for those targets, and he’s expected back in the lineup this week as he returns from a concussion. I’ve harped on this a bunch of times already, but last week’s game was mostly a non-factor for what I think of the Browns, except for one thing (I’ll get to that in a bit) due to the weather conditions.
