The Ravens rank 3rd in the NFL in rushing yards per game (164.4) and are also 3rd in yards per carry (5.07). Side note: It seems pretty stunning that with how poor the Browns’ rushing attack has been, they are ranked 21st in rushing yards per game . The Browns’ run defense is 18th in rushing yards allowed per game (117.4) and 23rd in rushing yards per play allowed (4.48). They allowed their first rushing touchdown of the season last week against a Jets rushing attack that had previously been anemic. For a team that has relied on close, last-second victories, I see that successful rushing attack for the Ravens being the defining factor this week in them taking over the game late. High Stakes for Cleveland The stakes couldn’t be higher for Cleveland this week. If they win, they go back into first place in the AFC North, and would have victories over two division rivals already. If they lose, they are suddenly two games back of first place, and without the tiebreaker, which really makes it like three games back. Here are some of the positives I can think of this week, along with some general notes: I liked what Isaiah Bond did in training camp, and it’s unfortunate that his time to shine came in rainy conditions, which likely contributed to a couple big dropped passes. With that said, KC Concepcion was meant for those targets, and he’s expected back in the lineup this week as he returns from a concussion. Zay Flowers is obviously a lot more proven than the rookie, but we’ll get to see each player on both sides (and a lot like to compare Todd Monken’s utilization of the two). If the defense can find a way to be better against the run, then certainly they pose a problem for Tyler Huntley (or anyone for that matter). Last week against Geno Smith , after that first drive, he practically could not get anything going. That is an important point to make, though: on that first drive, the team should lock up with Zay Flowers right away, because if the Browns don’t adjust in-between weeks, then those crossing routes will burn them early again. The eye test continues to tell me that Quinshon Judkins hasn’t been right this season. There was a time last season when he looked just as impressive as the rest of the team’s young rookie class, and even though he averaged 3.6 yards per carry, the eye test always said, ‘Man if our offensive line wasn’t so bad, I wonder what Judkins could do,’ because you saw the ability there. Now, everything is so pedestrian looking with his running style, that he looks like just another guy. Don’t get me wrong, there is plenty wrong with the blocking as well, but Judkins’ stock has fallen to the bottom of the pool in comparing the team’s promising young players. The offensive line took a step back in pass protection last week, but that’s one of those things I don’t get overly concerned with unless it happens in normal weather conditions. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 3 point underdogs against the Jets. The over/under is 39.5. Quick Hitters Offensive coordinator Travis Switzer was asked about the offensive line breakdown last week that led to a bunch of sacks, and how communication comes into play: “Yeah, it’s about taking every rep, whether it’s a walkthrough rep, a practice rep, it might be a meeting rep, where we’re just talking through things, and it’s making sure everybody’s on the same page and they’re hearing guys communicate, because they’re the ones out there that have to do it. Certainly, we kind of give them the guidelines, if you will, but communication is the priority there. I mean, even if they maybe didn’t do it exactly the way that we talked about it, if we’re all on the same page, we have a chance. So, I think it’s just taking advantage of every single possible rep you could get, whether it’s a walk, a practice, a meeting rep, and making sure everybody’s on the same page there.” Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg talked about making adjustments to the defense pretty quick last week after the Jets’ opening-drive score: “A game is like a week in practice. It’s like the Wednesday to the Thursday to the Friday. They say the first drive to the second drive, and you’re constantly trying to find your different edges. Eliminate Browns hurting Browns, eliminate things that could hurt us, build on things that could help us, figure out what they’re doing. ‘Oh, this can work, let’s go here.’ It’s a constant adjustment process, or it’s a constant, ‘hey, let’s settle back. Let’s let our players get their cleats in the ground, their eyes right, and play fast as hell.’ And every game, no matter the first drive, the third drive, the tenth drive, it’s a constant process of all of us together on the sideline just trying to figure out what’s best for the next drive and then don’t even think about anything after that. And shoot, whatever happens in that drive, what’s best for the next drive. And sometimes it is adjustments, sometimes it is just take a step back, let’s let our play style take over. So, it’s a credit to those guys, the way they responded. And also, part of that is just the heart, the resilience after a tough first drive to bounce back, is credit to our players.” Special teams coordinator Bryon Storer said both the long snapper and punter made mistakes on the game-costing punt last week: “Well, it started with the snap. We had a high snap. I talked to Rex (Sunahara), me and Rex watched the tape, and he brought his hips up, which brought the ball up, and then it slipped right through Corey’s hands. And so that was an unfortunate series of events on the one play. Usually those two guys, this was the eighth punt of the game, so they had done a pretty darn good job up to that point in the game. And for whatever reason, they both made a mistake on the same play. And usually when guys that handle the ball every single play that they’re out there, if both of those guys make a mistake, there’s going to be something bad that’s going to happen. That’s part of the job.” Here are predictions from multiple staff members at DBN: Predictions Chris Pokorny: “As I said earlier, I had to lean toward the Ravens this week. If the Jets were able to run all over the Browns last week with the defensive tackle issues, then Baltimore will do the same to them. Let’s hope that besides that, the Browns play a relatively clean game, minimizing turnovers, and getting a few clutch plays to give them a shot at the end of the game. Unfortunately, I think the Ravens will utilize that won’t be able to deter the mighty Ravens’ run game too much.” Ravens 23, Browns 17 Jared Mueller : “The injury issues with both teams tell me this will be a battle between RB Derrick Henry and QB Deshaun Watson. Can the Browns defense hold up without a few defensive linemen and, likely, LB Carson Schwesinger? Can Cleveland’s offense get things going without RBs Quinshon Judkins (likely) and Raheim Sanders (for sure)? item.title: Aqib Talib unloads on Ryan Fitzpatrick’s rant about Bo Nix: ‘You suck, bro!’
item.description: BOULDER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 29: Former NFL football cornerback Aqib Talib looks on from the sideline prior to the game between the Colorado Buffaloes and Oklahoma State Cowboys at Folsom Field on November 29, 2024 in Boulder, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former Denver Broncos cornerback Aqib Talib had some choice words for Ryan Fitzpatrick after he said Bo Nix is disrespectful to the quarterback position with his play against the Seattle Seahawks this week. Talib absolutely eviscerated Fitzpatrick’s comments and I am here for it. Aqib Talib responds to Ryan Fitzpatrick's rant about Bo Nix after the Broncos victory over the Seahawks on TNF Tell em @AqibTalib21 pic.twitter.com/A0ilMh3sBX — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 17, 2026 Zack Kelberman posted the full transcript of this clip on X and it is a line-by-line takedown of TNF’s talking head: “ You are disrespectful to the quarterback position ’cause you suck. Period. … We’re talking about a guy [Fitzpatrick] who played for nine different teams in 17 years. ’Cause ain’t nobody want his ass. We’re talking about a guy who only played for a team for more than two years once. That’s Buffalo. And his record as a starter in Buffalo was 19-35. That’s f*cking suck. “A guy who played 17 years, 147 starts, and never sniffed a playoff game. He never touched the playoffs ever. That’s disrespectful to the quarterback position. “You suck. You suck, bro. “We’re talking about a guy who got 169 interceptions, more interceptions than he has starts. How can a quarterback of his caliber talk about what is disrespectful to the quarterback position? Nobody’s worried about what Fitzpatrick said. Nobody was worried about playing against you. You suck.” Talib is probably the best former-player covering the Broncos in 2026. He gives it straight, but he also defends the team without feeding into the fan overreactions. And hey, I’m certainly one to overreact during and immediately after games. So I appreciate the straight-talk Talib dishes for fans sometimes too. At the end of the day, the Broncos are 4-2 and right where they hoped to be after those first six brutal games on their schedule. Sean Payton and Bo Nix will figure this out and the team is winning while they are.

item.title: GVSU has zero margin for error after couple costly plays come up short vs Ferris State | D'Addona
item.description: ALLENDALE - Grand Valley State football coach Scott Wooster knows the margin for error is zero the rest of the season. It is that way every year in the GLIAC for a team aiming for title contention. After losing back-to-back weeks to Michigan Tech and No. 1 Ferris State, the No. 13 Lakers can't afford another loss this season if they want to make the playoffs. Three losses didn't get GVSU in last year and it likely won't this season after a 41-34 loss to the rival Bulldogs on Saturday, Oct. 17. That is the charm and the curse of the GLIAC and the Anchor Bone Classic. The losing team of the rivalry game has very little margin for error. With Ferris State winning multiple NCAA titles in the past five years, GVSU's reign over the GLIAC seems just a little bit further back in history, and it has been 20 years since the Lakers won an NCAA championship. More: No. 1 Ferris State football overcomes early deficit to beat No. 13 GVSU "Our whole mentality and what I have been trying to get out of this building is that light work can be (the difference) in college football," Wooster said. "We had some guys think Michigan Tech would be light work and it got exposed. If we are the same every day regardless of the circumstances, we are going to win the football game. "That is what has to get out of this building for us to return to championship ball. It has been 20 years, and that is what has to get out of this building. I have not been able to get it out of this building yet - YET, but it is going to and we are going to be the same team every week. We are going to figure that out." It looked like the Lakers had it figured out in the first quarter. The Lakers grabbed two early turnovers (fumble recoveries by Tyus Jackson and Ryder Gravenhof) and had a big sack (Jackson) that put GVSU up 17-0 over rival Ferris State. "We got off to a great, great start. We had that belief right away," Wooster said. "This game has that momentum that comes in waves." The wave changed quickly in the second quarter. After playing elite defense in the first quarter and establishing a running game, everything screeched to a halt. The Lakers, which had 126 yards of offense in the first quarter managed just 2 in the second quarter. Two total yards of offense. And it wasn't like they had just one possession and the Bulldogs had the ball the entire time. GVSU had four possessions in the second quarter: Interception, three-and-out, fumble, three-and-out. After the interception, GVSU had plenty of chances to get things going but couldn't move the ball 2 yards the next three possessions. "(Ferris) did what we thought they were going to do the whole game, we just didn't execute," Schuster said. "We started hot and the defense played well the whole game. We didn't have their back in the middle (of the game)." We didn't have their back in the middle (of the game)." But Ferris State converted both turnovers and the first punt into 17 points to tie the game, the second TD and a field goal coming just 1:14 apart. "We have only turned the ball over twice all season (before the second quarter) and we let them get the momentum," Wooster said. "It was just (lack of) execution, pure and simple. We have to get the execution fixed. That is 100% on us." On the other side of the ball, GVSU's defense couldn't contain the running game, led by quarterback Wyatt Bower. Missed tackles and wide-open holes in the line that weren't there early in the game were all of a sudden a regular occurrence. It moved into the second half as Ferris State took the second-half kickoff and marched right down the field and scored twice to push the lead to 34-17. That made it 34 unanswered points before the Lakers finally struck again on a 61-yard Kellen Reed touchdown catch. But the Bulldogs turned right around less than a minute and a half later and answered with a quarterback run by Wyatt Bower that went 53 yards for a score. The Lakers didn't give up, scoring a field goal and a Schuster pass to Kellen Russell-Dixon for a touchdown that pulled them stunningly back within one score. But the Lakers ran out of time and now have to be nearly flawless to get to the next step of being a championship team again. Contact sports editor Dan D’Addona at Dan.D’Addona@hollandsentinel.com. item.title: Sahel states restart dialogue with ECOWAS
item.description: Three junta-ruled Sahel states on Saturday resumed dialogue with the ECOWAS regional bloc which they quit over 18 months ago, agreeing to work together towards a cooperation “framework agreement”. Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso, led by juntas that came to power between 2020 and 2023, left the Economic Community of West African States in January 2025, after teaming up to create their own group, the Alliance of Sahel States (AES). Talks between ECOWAS and the AES had been under way since January 2025 but Saturday was their first official ministerial meeting. In a joint statement issued Saturday evening, the two sides “welcomed the spirit of fraternity, mutual respect and openness” of the talks, and stressed the importance of maintaining relations of “good neighbourliness” particularly with “respect for sovereignty”. They agreed to “set up joint thematic working groups (…) to reach a framework cooperation agreement”. The AES delegation was led by Karamoko Jean-Marie Traore, Burkina Faso’s foreign minister, and the Ecowas delegation by Cheikh Niang, his Senegalese counterpart. The AES juntas have all turned their backs on France, the former colonial power, and by extension on several countries in the region such as Cete d’Ivoire and Benin, which they consider too close to Paris. The trio have moved closer politically to Moscow, claiming an anti-imperialist and pro-sovereignty vision, and they have bitterly criticised west African coastal countries which have remained close to France. The post Sahel states restart dialogue with ECOWAS appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Dubois destroys Wardley in round two to retain WBO heavyweight crown
item.description: Daniel Dubois scored a crushing second-round knockout victory over fellow Briton Fabio Wardley to retain his World Boxing Organization heavyweight crown on Saturday. In a much-anticipated rematch of their bruising 11-round classic earlier this year, Dubois dominated Wardley from the opening bell to batter his rival into submission in the second round. Dubois dropped Wardley after 17 seconds of the contest at the O2 Arena in London, catching the challenger flush on the chin with a huge overhand right. The 29-year-old Dubois continued to land punches at will throughout the first round, which finished with Wardley clinging on desperately under a barrage a punches on the ropes. The second round started as the first had ended, with the 6ft 5in Dubois uncorking an array of punches that left Wardley in desperate trouble. With Dubois unloading on a defenceless Wardley, the towel came in after two minutes and 21 seconds of the round. Dubois improved to 24-3-0 with 23 knockouts while the 31-year-old Wardley fell to 20-2-1. AFP The post Dubois destroys Wardley in round two to retain WBO heavyweight crown appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Scottish Premiership: Rangers miss chance to go top after pulsating draw with Dundee
item.description: Jones equaliser denies Rangers victory Kilmarnock beat Motherwell 3-2 to move off bottom Rangers passed up the chance to go top of the Premiership in a pulsating 2-2 draw against Dundee at Dens Park. The home side took a deserved lead in the 38th minute through the striker Bradley Fink but the returning Gers attacker Badredine Bouanani fired in a stunning equaliser three minutes later with his first goal for the club. Derek McInnes’s side came out re-energised for the second half and took the lead on the hour with the midfielder Nico Raskin’s long-range drive but in the 68th minute the midfielder Callum Jones took advantage of Gers slackness to level. Dundee were well worth a point, with Rangers moving one point behind Celtic, who can increase their lead at home to Hearts on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Ambassador Dele Cole devoted his life to national service — Tinubu
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu has expressed sadness over the death of the veteran journalist and diplomat, Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, saying that the late statesman devoted his life to national service. Ambassador Cole died at the age of 86. President Tinubu, in his tribute titled “Farewell to Ambassador Dele Cole, distinguished diplomat, journalist and public servant,” said the late veteran journalist brought distinction to his work in diplomacy, journalism and politics. The tribute read: “I received with profound sadness the news of the passing of Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, a distinguished diplomat, journalist, politician, and public servant, who died at 86. “Ambassador Cole devoted his life to national service, bringing distinction to his work in diplomacy, journalism and politics. “His career reflected the enduring value of dialogue, tact, mutual respect and the pursuit of shared interests in advancing national development and international cooperation. “His contributions to Nigeria’s media landscape were particularly notable. As Managing Director of the Daily Times, he upheld the vital role of the press in holding public officials accountable, speaking truth to power, and strengthening democratic governance. His legacy in journalism and public life remains an enduring part of our national story. “At 86, Ambassador Dele Cole witnessed defining moments in Nigeria’s history and contributed to the nation’s development through his work in the media, diplomacy and public service. His life stands as a testament to the value of experience, principled engagement and commitment to the public good. “As we mourn his passing, I extend my heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, professional associates and all whose lives he touched. I pray that memories of his remarkable life will bring them comfort and strength at this difficult time. “May Almighty God grant Ambassador Cole eternal rest and give his family and all who mourn him the fortitude to bear this profound loss.” The post Ambassador Dele Cole devoted his life to national service — Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 19 Dead, 25 Hurt In Stampede At India Religious Gathering
item.description: At least 19 people were killed and two dozen more injured Saturday in eastern India after a stampede that occurred during sudden rainfall at a Hindu religious gathering, officials and Indian media said. West Bengal’s Chief Minister Suvendhu Adhikari told reporters the fatalities included a seven-year-old girl, adding that 25 other people were injured outside a pavilion “in a stampede” at the Hindu festival of Durga Puja in the city of Kolkata. “Six bodies have so far been identified,” Adhikari said. A senior police official at the scene told AFP an announcement caused “commotion” after it started raining at night and the “crowd waiting outside the pandal (pavilion) was pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede.” Afterwards, medics were seen moving injured people on stretchers, including a police officer, into a local hospital. Several relatives of victims cried and held one another as they mourned the loss of loved ones. Medical workers move an injured police officer on a stretcher, following the Durga Puja Pandal stampede, in front of the emergency building of Calcutta Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata on October 16, 2026. Photo by STRINGER / AFP Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the tragedy in a short statement on Facebook. “The stampede in Kolkata is saddening. Condolences to the bereaved families. Wishing the injured a speedy recovery,” he wrote. “The West Bengal Government is providing all possible help to the affected families.” Adhikari originally announced 17 fatalities. The Press Trust of India (PTI) reported the death toll rose by two to 19, quoting Adhikari in a later statement. Nine dead bodies have been released to their families, the PTI reported. It also said police have taken the closed circuit footage of the festival and authorities would initiate action against those seen on CCTV who appeared to fail in their responsibility for crowd control. Videos shot before the stampede appeared to show large crowds of people waiting to enter the pavilion, in an area with narrow lanes that allow only a few people to walk in at a time, according to Indian Express. Deadly crowd incidents are a frequent occurrence at Indian mass events, such as religious festivals, due to poor management and safety lapses. Last year, a stampede at India’s Kumbh Mela religious fair killed 30 people and injured several others, and 11 fans were crushed to death in Bengaluru during celebrations for the local cricket team’s first Indian Premier League title. The same year, 36 people were killed after a stampede broke out at a campaign rally of a popular actor-turned-politician in southern Tamil Nadu state. In 2024, 121 people were killed in northern Uttar Pradesh state during a Hindu religious gathering. item.content:encoded: At least 19 people were killed and two dozen more injured Saturday in eastern India after a stampede that occurred during sudden rainfall at a Hindu religious gathering, officials and Indian media said. West Bengal’s Chief Minister Suvendhu Adhikari told reporters the fatalities included a seven-year-old girl, adding that 25 other people were injured outside a pavilion “in a stampede” at the Hindu festival of Durga Puja in the city of Kolkata. “Six bodies have so far been identified,” Adhikari said. A senior police official at the scene told AFP an announcement caused “commotion” after it started raining at night and the “crowd waiting outside the pandal (pavilion) was pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede.” Afterwards, medics were seen moving injured people on stretchers, including a police officer, into a local hospital. item.title: Nigeria’s economy needs continuation of Tinubu’s reforms – Wike
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says Nigeria’s full economic recovery depends entirely on sustaining the bold reform policies initiated by President Bola Tinubu. Wike said this on Saturday, at the Rainbow Coalition’s stakeholders’ consultation in Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area of Rivers. He said that only the continuation of the current administration’s economic direction could permanently pull the country back from the brink of collapse. He noted that the hard economic choices being implemented presently were necessary remedies to salvage a system that was virtually “dead” when Tinubu took office. “Only the continuation of the economic reforms initiated by the Tinubu government can bring this country back from the economic comatose it was in before this present administration took over,” he said. He said that the presidential candidate of the Africa Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Abubakar Atiku and his vice, Rotimi Amaechi, had nothing to offer to Nigerians. The minister urged residents of the state not to surrender the country’s progress to “career politicians” and “political opportunists” whom he likened to “chronic pool betters” who repeatedly gamble with public trust. According to him, supporting politicians who have made decades-long pursuits for power would mean diverting national funds to recoup lost campaign expenses rather than consolidating economic gains. Wike further said that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, would not make any meaningful difference if elected, stressing that Tinubu was the person who had shown true commitment. Reaffirming that leadership must be judged by past governance records, the former Rivers governor challenged his predecessor to account for major capital allocations in Rivers. Explaining the political strategy behind the cross-party Rainbow Coalition movement, he said that delivering economic recovery required total alignment between the executive and the national assembly. He urged voters to support Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates vying for the Senate and House of Representatives seats in the area to ensure legislative cooperation for the president’s economic policy agenda. He also called on party leaders and community mobilisers to prepare for an overwhelming turnout on election day. “I want total mobilisation on Jan. 16, 2027. Everybody must be mobilised. item.title: FG Warns Return Of Fuel Subsidy Can Trigger Capital Flight
item.description: The Federal Government has warned that a return to the fuel subsidy can trigger capital flight, put pressure on the naira, and undermine the gains of its economic reforms. The warning came at a media briefing in Bangkok, Thailand, at the conclusion of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings. The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele; the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, Olayemi Cardoso; and the Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Atiku Bagudu, addressed Nigeria’s economic outlook following the conclusion of the meeting. Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy Taiwo Oyedele said on October 8, 2026, that FG’s 30-day fuel reduction is not a return of the subsidy. The finance minister said investors have repeatedly sought assurances that the government will not reverse the removal of fuel subsidy or the unification of exchange rates, particularly as the country approaches another election cycle. Oyedele argued that any signal of a possible return to subsidies could prompt investors to withdraw their capital, putting pressure on the foreign exchange market and the naira. The Minister of Finance and the Central Bank Governor arrive for the final briefing by the Nigerian delegation to the 2026 IMF-World Bank Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. After five days of deliberations, the delegation highlighted some of the key takeaways from the event, especially as they impact the administration’s economic policies. ﻿ It clarified the decision to discount the retail price of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS). The delegation also announced the Federal Government’s seven per cent economic growth target. In his remarks, the Minister of Budget and Economic Planning emphasised the need for fiscal and monetary authorities to work together to sustain the gains of the reforms. Debt, climate, AI, and inequality topped the agenda at the World Bank-IMF meeting attended by Nigeria and 190 other countries in Thailand. At the meeting, Nigeria called for comprehensive reforms of the IMF and the World Bank to give developing economies a strong voice in global financial decisions, improve access to financing and strengthen their capacity to withstand economic shocks. While presenting the Group of Twenty-Four (G-24) 2026 annual meeting communiqué in Bangkok, Thailand, on the sidelines of the World Bank/IMF Annual Meetings, Oyedele said geopolitical conflicts, trade uncertainties, volatile commodity prices and climate shocks are threatening global economic growth. According to him, the challenges disproportionately affect emerging markets and developing economies, undermining efforts to create jobs and achieve inclusive transformation. The post FG Warns Return Of Fuel Subsidy Can Trigger Capital Flight appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Hunters kill two suspected bandits, recover ₦10m ransom in Kano
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Two suspected bandits have been killed by local hunters, while ₦10 million paid as ransom for a kidnapped man has been recovered in Falgore Forest, Doguwa Local Government Area of Kano State. This was contained in a statement signed by CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, Police Public Relations Officer, on Saturday. According to the statement, the kidnapped victim, identified as 45-year-old Kabiru Aliyu of Falgore Village, was released unharmed after the suspects collected the ransom The incident occurred at about midnight on Saturday, when three suspected bandits allegedly emerged from Falgore Forest to collect the money demanded for Aliyu’s release. According to the statement, the victim was kidnapped on September 11, 2026, and had spent several days in captivity before his release. The police said that shortly after collecting the ₦10 million ransom and releasing the victim, the suspects were ambushed by local hunters known as Yan Bula while returning to their hideout in Falgore Forest. “During the ambush, two of the suspected bandits were neutralised, while the third suspect escaped with injuries. The entire ransom sum of ₦10 million was recovered intact from the neutralised suspects,” the statement said. The command said preliminary investigations had identified one of the suspects killed as Dogo Isah, a commercial motorcycle rider from Maigwanda Village in Kubau Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The police said the suspects were believed to have come from Maigwanda Village before the incident. The Commissioner of Police in Kano State, CP Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, commended the Yan Bula hunters for their efforts in supporting security operations in the area. Bakori said the hunters’ activities continued to complement the police operation against kidnapping, banditry and other violent crimes in the state under Operation Kukan Kura. Following the incident, the commissioner directed the Area Commander, Divisional Police Officers and tactical teams operating in the area to immediately search the forest and surrounding communities for the fleeing suspect. He also directed the teams to intensify efforts to arrest the suspect and recover any weapons used by the group. The police further disclosed that the rescued victim had been debriefed, medically examined and reunited with his family. The command assured residents of its commitment to protecting lives and property. The post Hunters kill two suspected bandits, recover ₦10m ransom in Kano appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Five Things To Know — What Has Changed Since This Morning?
item.description: The evening picture is becoming clearer. The most consequential fresh development is the Federal Government’s reaffirmation of its economic reform policy despite pressure over petrol prices. Internationally, new warnings about debt, AI investment and development financing deserve attention. 1. Nigeria: Government rules out restoring petrol subsidies This photo shows an attendant holding a petrol nozzle. What happened: Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele said on Saturday that Nigeria will not return to petrol subsidies or multiple exchange rates, warning that reversing reforms could undermine investor confidence. He described the temporary NNPC retail discount as a commercial reduction in margins, rather than a return to government-funded subsidies. Why it matters: This clarifies the government’s policy position at a time when rising petrol costs are putting pressure on households and businesses. Strategic implications : The administration is prioritising policy continuity, while the unresolved question is how quickly lower inflation and stronger macroeconomic indicators translate into improved purchasing power. Watch next : Pump prices, transport fares, labour’s response and whether the government introduces further targeted relief. 2. Nigeria’s economy: Inflation eases, but the cost-of-living problem persists What happened: The latest official figures show September headline inflation falling to 14.63 per cent, from 15.39 per cent in August. Food inflation, however, remained elevated at 19.59 per cent. Reuters reported that Nigerians continue to experience substantial pressure from transport and everyday expenses. Why it matters: Lower inflation means prices are generally rising more slowly, not necessarily falling. This distinction will be central to assessments of Nigeria’s economic progress. Business implications: High food and transport costs continue to constrain consumer spending, while lower policy interest rates may gradually improve financing conditions. Watch next: October inflation, petrol prices and evidence of lower commercial borrowing costs. 3. Election security: Army chief visits Borno after presidential directive Shaibu What happened: Chief of Army Staff Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu arrived in Maiduguri on Saturday following President Tinubu’s directive to security agencies to intensify efforts to rescue abducted Nigerians and dismantle terrorist and bandit camps. The President also instructed security chiefs to ensure a secure environment for January’s elections. Why it matters: Security is an important operational condition for credible elections, particularly in areas affected by insurgency and kidnapping. Strategic implications: The effectiveness of these directives will depend on measurable improvements in security, not the announcement alone. The most consequential fresh development is the Federal Government’s reaffirmation of its economic reform policy despite pressure over petrol prices. Internationally, new warnings about debt, AI investment and development financing deserve attention. 1. Nigeria: Government rules out restoring petrol subsidies This photo shows an attendant holding a petrol nozzle. What happened: Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele said on Saturday that Nigeria will not return to petrol subsidies or multiple exchange rates, warning that reversing reforms could undermine investor confidence. He described the temporary NNPC retail discount as a commercial reduction in margins, rather than a return to government-funded subsidies. Why it matters: This clarifies the government’s policy position at a time when rising petrol costs are putting pressure on households and businesses. Strategic implications : The administration is prioritising policy continuity, while the unresolved question is how quickly lower inflation and stronger macroeconomic indicators translate into improved purchasing power. Watch next : Pump prices, transport fares, labour’s response and whether the government introduces further targeted relief. 2. Nigeria’s economy: Inflation eases, but the cost-of-living problem persists What happened: The latest official figures show September headline inflation falling to 14.63 per cent, from 15.39 per cent in August. Food inflation, however, remained elevated at 19.59 per cent. Reuters reported that Nigerians continue to experience substantial pressure from transport and everyday expenses. Why it matters: Lower inflation means prices are generally rising more slowly, not necessarily falling. This distinction will be central to assessments of Nigeria’s economic progress. Business implications: High food and transport costs continue to constrain consumer spending, while lower policy interest rates may gradually improve financing conditions. Watch next: October inflation, petrol prices and evidence of lower commercial borrowing costs. 3. Election security: Army chief visits Borno after presidential directive Shaibu What happened: Chief of Army Staff Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu arrived in Maiduguri on Saturday following President Tinubu’s directive to security agencies to intensify efforts to rescue abducted Nigerians and dismantle terrorist and bandit camps. The President also instructed security chiefs to ensure a secure environment for January’s elections. Why it matters: Security is an important operational condition for credible elections, particularly in areas affected by insurgency and kidnapping. Strategic implications: The effectiveness of these directives will depend on measurable improvements in security, not the announcement alone. Watch next: Rescue operations, security assessments in vulnerable constituencies and the deployment plans agreed between INEC and security agencies. 4. Africa and development: Debt pressures threaten investment and jobs A file photo of the World Bank headquarters in Washington, DC What happened: Reuters reported Saturday that developing countries’ external debt has reached approximately $12.3 trillion, while official development assistance fell 23 per cent in 2025. World Bank President Ajay Banga is advocating greater mobilisation of private capital as governments face growing pressure to finance infrastructure and employment. Why it matters: Debt servicing is competing with spending on electricity, education, healthcare and transport across developing economies. Business opportunities and risks: Development-finance guarantees, blended finance and public-private partnerships may become increasingly important for African infrastructure. However, high borrowing costs make poorly structured projects particularly vulnerable. Watch next: New financing commitments emerging from the IMF–World Bank meetings, debt-relief initiatives and support for African infrastructure. 5. Technology and AI: Industry leaders warn that regulation is lagging innovation Artificial Intelligence What happened: Speaking at the IMF–World Bank meetings, Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark argued that rapid improvements in artificial intelligence could transform productivity and economic growth. He also warned that governments may be running out of time to establish effective safeguards against cybersecurity threats, biological misuse, and other risks. His company’s very large estimates of potential economic gains remain projections, not independently established outcomes. Why it matters: AI is becoming a major economic-policy issue, not merely a technology-industry concern. Media and business implications: Broadcasters face two parallel opportunities: using AI to improve production and distribution, and negotiating fair compensation when technology platforms use original journalism. Watch next: International AI regulation, news-content licensing agreements, enterprise adoption and whether investment produces measurable productivity gains. Saturday Evening’s Strategic Takeaway The clearest change since the morning briefing is the government’s renewed commitment to maintaining market-oriented economic reforms despite pressure over fuel prices. The most important developing domestic issue is security ahead of the elections. Military deployments and operational directives now need to translate into verifiable results For broadcasting and digital investment, the emerging international debate over AI regulation, intellectual property and financing remains particularly significant. item.title: Benue 2027: Ex-Otukpo council chair, APC, ADC, ZLP chieftains defect to PDP
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A former Caretaker Chairman of Otukpo Local Government Area of Benue state, Mr. Inalegwu Adakonye, has defected from the All Progressives Congress (APC) to the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), alongside other political stakeholders and their supporters from the APC, African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Zenith Labour Party (ZLP). The defection featured several prominent political figures from Adoka and Ugboju communities in Otukpo council. Among prominent politicians who weekend in Otukpo joined the PDP with the former chairman of Otukpo were Adoga Edache, popularly known as Ebo, from the ADC; Emmanuel Akoche of the ZLP; Garuba Sule of the APC; and Mr. John Ojonye, ADC Chairman of Ugboju Ehaji Ward, alongside other party members and supporters. Explaining his decision to return to the PDP, Adakonye said the party’s ideology of inclusiveness and collective participation informed his choice, arguing that its approach to politics differed from that of the APC. He said “the PDP treats its members as one family and offer a platform where everyone can participate. And I am confident that the party is best positioned to rescue Benue state from bad governance.” Adakonye, who led APC members from Adoka and Ugboju into the PDP, also cited the emergence of Dr. Oyije Ogbenjuwa as the party’s deputy governorship candidate as a factor behind their decision. He said they could not afford to remain outside the political movement of their brother and friend, who he expressed confidence would soon become the deputy governor of the state. The defectors also cited the PDP’s people-oriented ideology, leadership and prospects in forthcoming elections as reasons for abandoning their former parties for the opposition platform. Receiving the new members were the PDP deputy governorship candidate, Dr. Ogbenjuwa; the Otukpo Local Government PDP Chairman, Godwin Ochapa; the party’s House of Assembly candidate for Otukpo/Akpa, Johnson Egli; its candidate for Adoka/Ugboju, Gabriel Olofu; and the Senior Legislative Aide to the Senate President, Chief George Alli. item.title: 5 Years Later, One Game’s Blood Sacrifice Mechanic Still Haunts Me
item.description: Typically, when you’re playing a card game, the stakes aren’t that high. Perhaps you’ve got some money on the line. Maybe bragging rights are on the table. But even if you lose, largely speaking, things are going to be fine. Not so in 2021’s Inscryption , a deckbuilder horror game developed by Daniel Mullins Games and published by Devolver Digital, that starts with a haunted card game in a creepy cabin in the woods. But before long, you’ll be eyeing a pair of pliers and wondering which parts of your own body you can live without.

item.title: ‎Niger State Miners’ Deaths: Suspended NSCDC Commandant Admits ‘Costly Mistake’, Apologises To Bereaved Families
item.description: ‎‎ ‎The suspended Niger State Commandant of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Suberu Aniviye, has admitted that the deaths of suspected illegal miners in the corps’ custody could have been prevented, describing the incident as a “costly mistake” and apologising to the bereaved families and the Niger State Government. ‎ ‎The admission came as the Justice Muhammad Muhammad Commission of Inquiry in Minna heard testimony that the command’s legal officer had advised the former commandant to release minors arrested during the operation to their parents on bail. ﻿ ‎ ‎Aniviye tendered the apology while testifying before the commission, which is investigating the circumstances surrounding the deaths of detainees in NSCDC custody in September 2026. ‎ ‎“A mistake has been made, but a very costly one. My apology to the parents of the deceased and to the people and government of Niger State,” he told the commission. ‎ ‎The former state commandant expressed regret that the incident occurred during his tenure, acknowledging that the deaths could have been avoided. ‎ ‎He told the commission that he assumed duty as Niger State NSCDC Commandant on August 25, 2025, and remained in office until September 18, 2026. ‎ ‎According to him, the operation at a mining site along the M. I. Wushishi Housing Estate in Minna followed written and oral complaints from residents who alleged that mining activities were disrupting their community. ‎ ‎Aniviye said he visited the site on September 15, 2026, and subsequently directed the command’s Head of Operations, Assistant Commandant of Corps Joha Achagwa, to act on the complaints. ‎ ‎He explained that the Mining Marshal Unit was deployed, leading to the arrest of suspected illegal miners during an operation on the evening of September 16. ‎ ‎The following day, however, several detainees were reported dead in the corps’ custody. ‎ ‎Aniviye told the commission that he received a telephone call informing him that some suspects had died in detention, prompting him to rush to the command headquarters, where he found several bodies lying on the floor of the cell. ‎ ‎He said he contacted Niger State Governor, Umaru Bago, who directed that the bodies be taken to a hospital. item.dc:creator: Alexander Okere
item.content:encoded: ‎‎ ‎The suspended Niger State Commandant of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Suberu Aniviye, has admitted that the deaths of suspected illegal miners in the corps’ custody could have been prevented, describing the incident as a “costly mistake” and apologising to the bereaved families and the Niger State Government. ‎ ‎The admission came as the Justice Muhammad Muhammad Commission of Inquiry in Minna heard testimony that the command’s legal officer had advised the former commandant to release minors arrested during the operation to their parents on bail. ﻿ ‎ ‎Aniviye tendered the apology while testifying before the commission, which is investigating the circumstances surrounding the deaths of detainees in NSCDC custody in September 2026. ‎ ‎“A mistake has been made, but a very costly one. My apology to the parents of the deceased and to the people and government of Niger State,” he told the commission. ‎ ‎The former state commandant expressed regret that the incident occurred during his tenure, acknowledging that the deaths could have been avoided. ‎ ‎He told the commission that he assumed duty as Niger State NSCDC Commandant on August 25, 2025, and remained in office until September 18, 2026. ‎ ‎According to him, the operation at a mining site along the M. I. Wushishi Housing Estate in Minna followed written and oral complaints from residents who alleged that mining activities were disrupting their community. ‎ ‎Aniviye said he visited the site on September 15, 2026, and subsequently directed the command’s Head of Operations, Assistant Commandant of Corps Joha Achagwa, to act on the complaints. ‎ ‎He explained that the Mining Marshal Unit was deployed, leading to the arrest of suspected illegal miners during an operation on the evening of September 16. ‎ ‎The following day, however, several detainees were reported dead in the corps’ custody. ‎ ‎Aniviye told the commission that he received a telephone call informing him that some suspects had died in detention, prompting him to rush to the command headquarters, where he found several bodies lying on the floor of the cell. ‎ ‎He said he contacted Niger State Governor, Umaru Bago, who directed that the bodies be taken to a hospital. Aniviye added that he also informed the Commissioner of Police and the Director of the Department of State Services about the incident. ‎ ‎The suspended commandant further disclosed that arrangements had been made to arraign the suspects in court on September 17 before the deaths occurred. ‎ ‎However, testimony by the suspended head of the NSCDC legal unit, Assistant Commandant of Corps Stephen Tsado, raised further questions about the treatment of the detainees and the handling of minors arrested during the operation. ‎ ‎Tsado, whose responsibilities included preparing case files, forwarding cases for prosecution and advising the commandant on legal matters, said he noticed that some of the arrested suspects were minors and advised Aniviye to release them to their parents on bail. ‎ ‎He told the commission that he personally urged the commandant to act on his advice to protect the rights of the minors but could not explain why the recommendation was not implemented. ‎ ‎“I advised him to grant them bail to their parents,” Tsado said. ‎ ‎The commission also heard testimony from Nurse Maryam Etang of the NSCDC medical unit, who said she visited the detention cell as part of her routine duties on September 16 and 17. ‎ ‎Etang disclosed that one of the suspects was coughing seriously on September 17, around the time the bodies were being removed from the cell. ‎ ‎She also said she was shocked to discover the body of one Emeka Emmanuel among those removed, insisting that he was not among the miners arrested during the operation. ‎ ‎Her testimony raised further questions about Emmanuel’s presence in the cell and the circumstances that led to his death. ‎ ‎The commission is expected to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths, examine the treatment of the detainees and determine whether there were lapses in the conduct of the operation and the subsequent handling of those in custody. ‎ ‎In earlier proceedings, a mortician at the Minna General Hospital told the commission that 33 bodies were delivered to the hospital’s mortuary, a figure that differs from the 37 deaths reported by the Niger State Government and other authorities. Governor Umaru Bago in September inaugurated a nine-member judicial commission of inquiry to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths of 37 miners in the custody of the NSCDC in the state. The deaths of the miners triggered a protest in the state, prompting Governor Bago to declare a 24-hour curfew in Minna, the state capital. Following the tragedy, President Bola Tinubu ordered a full and transparent investigation, saying that the government would not tolerate mass deaths arising from official negligence, dereliction of duty, or failure by public officials to protect the lives placed under their care. Similarly, the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, announced the suspension of 20 NSCDC officers in connection with the deaths. The post ‎Niger State Miners’ Deaths: Suspended NSCDC Commandant Admits ‘Costly Mistake’, Apologises To Bereaved Families appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: How my mother was kidnapped over $2.4bn subsidy fraud — Okonjo-Iweala
item.description: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, the Director-General of the World Trade Organisation, WTO, has recalled how her investigation into an alleged $2.4bn fuel subsidy fraud in Nigeria led her mother’s kidnapping. Read Also: Okonjo-Iweala’s mother, 82, kidnapped Okonjo-Iweala narrated her experience in an interview with Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua. She said the kidnappers’ demands were that she resigns as the Minister of Finance and leave the country. On how the ordeal began, she said her office noticed a sharp increase in subsidy claims, so she began to probe. Her words: “So I went to the president and said, look, something is going on here. Could we audit the accounts? And he said, yes, go ahead. “And we found about $2.4 billion worth of fraud. So we refused to pay.” That was when they took her mother. Okonjo-Iweala said the five-day ordeal was among the most painful periods of her life. “I was told (by the kidnappers) that for her to be released, I should resign and leave the country. “She was held in the middle of a forest, and one night she escaped. She’s still alive. She’s 96 now.” “It was a terrible, terrible five-day ordeal. I think the worst in my life,” she said. Okonjo-Iweala said initially she felt paralysed by fear and considered resigning. She added that that the experience left her with a sense of guilt that she still carries. “I never dreamt my parents could ever be touched in this way, that people would be that evil,” she said. On her father’s reaction at the time, she said: “He said, ‘We don’t give in to blackmail’. And he said, ‘You’ve got to carry on. You’ve got to go to work’.” Okonjo-Iweala served as Minister of Finance under President Goodluck Jonathan. Her mother, Kamene Okonjo, was kidnapped from her home in Ogwashi-Uku, Delta State, in December 2012. Read the kidnap story HERE . Vanguard News The post How my mother was kidnapped over $2.4bn subsidy fraud — Okonjo-Iweala appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Zulum calls for coordinated military offensive in the Lake Chad
item.description: …Zulum’s support instrumental to military success – COAS By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has called on the military to immediately commence a coordinated offensive operation, Operation Lake Sanity, to dislodge insurgents from the shores and islands of Lake Chad. Governor Zulum made the call on Saturday when he received the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shuaibu, on a courtesy visit at the new Council Chamber, Government House, Maiduguri. The governor commended the Nigerian Army for improvements in the security situation in the state and also requested stronger military deployments in strategic locations, including Kareto, Baga, and the Sabon Gari–Wajiroko axis, to protect communities, secure waterways, and support the reopening of the Damboa–Biu road. “The recent attacks on some communities in northern Borno are a result of the presence of insurgents along the shores of Lake Chad. We cannot achieve complete peace without undertaking major military operations in that area,” Zulum said. The governor acknowledged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s support for the proposed operation and the coordination among the service chiefs; however, he urged the military authorities to accelerate preparations. “I understand that the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, has provided the necessary support for the operation. I urge you to hasten the process so that the insurgents threatening northern Borno can be dislodged,” he stated. He called for strengthening the amphibious command in Baga to clear waterways, stressing that holding those positions would be essential to sustaining the operation’s gains. On the Gubio–Damasak corridor, Zulum appealed for the speedy establishment of a military formation in Kareto, and around Sabon Gari and Wajiroko in Damboa Local Government Area to support the restoration of vehicular movement between Damboa and Biu. Governor Babagana Zulum thanked the Chief of Army Staff for training about 1,000 forest guards, who he said had completed their training and were deployed to the state. Zulum emphasised the need to consolidate military successes through reconstruction, rehabilitation and resettlement, commending the Army’s support for re-establishing the Mairari community and preparing for military formations and community resettlement in Maiwa, Koshobe and Ala. “Military operations must be followed by stabilisation measures, including reconstruction, rehabilitation and resettlement. We cannot achieve complete peace without undertaking major military operations in that area,” Zulum said. The governor acknowledged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s support for the proposed operation and the coordination among the service chiefs; however, he urged the military authorities to accelerate preparations. “I understand that the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, has provided the necessary support for the operation. I urge you to hasten the process so that the insurgents threatening northern Borno can be dislodged,” he stated. He called for strengthening the amphibious command in Baga to clear waterways, stressing that holding those positions would be essential to sustaining the operation’s gains. On the Gubio–Damasak corridor, Zulum appealed for the speedy establishment of a military formation in Kareto, and around Sabon Gari and Wajiroko in Damboa Local Government Area to support the restoration of vehicular movement between Damboa and Biu. Governor Babagana Zulum thanked the Chief of Army Staff for training about 1,000 forest guards, who he said had completed their training and were deployed to the state. Zulum emphasised the need to consolidate military successes through reconstruction, rehabilitation and resettlement, commending the Army’s support for re-establishing the Mairari community and preparing for military formations and community resettlement in Maiwa, Koshobe and Ala. “Military operations must be followed by stabilisation measures, including reconstruction, rehabilitation and resettlement. Borno State Government will provide the support required by the Nigerian Army to fortify these locations,” he pledged. He also expressed appreciation for additional battalions deployed across the two sectors, noting that the reinforcements were helping to strengthen security and stabilise affected areas. “Notwithstanding the recent attacks in some parts of Borno State, there has been tremendous improvement in our security situation. I commend the officers and men of Operation Hadin Kai and urge them to sustain this momentum,” Zulum announced. The Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shuaibu, commended Governor Babagana Umara Zulum for his sustained support to the Nigerian Army, describing it as instrumental to the successes recorded against insurgency. “I must put on record that the support of the Executive Governor of Borno State has been phenomenal in the successes we have recorded here in Borno State. For that, we say a very big thank you, sir,” the COAS said. The Army Chief explained that his visit to troops of Operation Hadin Kai was part of a routine assessment of their operations, to encourage commanders, and to appreciate the resilience of personnel confronting insurgency in the Northeast. He reaffirmed their mandate to restore normalcy and create an enabling environment for socio-economic activities, assuring that challenges presented by commanders would receive prompt attention. The courtesy visit was attended by the Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, member representing Marte, Monguno, Nganzai federal constituency, Hon. Bukar Talba, Secretary to the State Government, Commissioners, Special Advisers and other senior military and heads of security establishment in the state. item.title: To suggest Anthony Kila hasn’t gone to school is stupid — Utomi
item.description: Political Economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, says he cannot guarantee that embattled professor Anthony Kila has never made mistakes but to suggest that he has never gone to school is spectacularly unfair to his personality. Utomi made this known on his verified Facebook page in Lagos on Saturday, saying that Kila is a good man. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) recalls that Kila is currently at the centre of a major scandal regarding his academic credentials. In October, an investigative report published by Premium Times revealed that Kila allegedly falsified all of his higher education qualifications, including his bachelor’s, master’s, doctorate (PhD) degrees, and his rank as a professor. Utomi, reacting to the online claim, said that there was no evidence to support the claim that Anthony Kila (popularly known as “Prof Kila”) had never gone to school. “I know Anthony Kila. I became aware of all the trending discussions about his career rather late. “I have never had any reason to ask about his certificates or letters of appointment, so I cannot claim to have those details. “However, if he has never gone to school, then those who have must ask for a refund. “We watched the cyber mob bully Jason Arday, the youngest Black professor ever appointed at Cambridge, to his early death. “Incidentally, I first met Anthony Kila in the city of Cambridge, England, in 2006, when I was beginning a run for the office of President of Nigeria.” Utomi said that among those in the mob that sought to lynch Arday were white professors, who had been pardoned for mistakes of a far worse nature. He said he did not know who might be going after Kila in a country where many people confer academic and non-academic titles on themselves, while the media, through its status-conferring function, elevates them to celebrity status. He, however, said that this does not seem normal, saying he could empathise because he has had a similar experience. Utomi said: “Years ago, when a journalist tried to suggest that my stay at Volkswagen Nigeria had something to do with its demise, I offered ₦12 million to anyone who could produce a shred of evidence to support that claim. Fifteen years on, no one has come forward to claim the bounty. “When I became the first professor of Pan-African (Pan-Atlantic) parent of the Lagos Business School, someone at UNILAG went, “…huh, until he found out that the evaluating team was led by the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ibadan.” “If professors like Adele Jinadu in Political Science and Joe Umo at UNILAG had not met me in graduate school abroad and interacted with my Head of Department, Elinor Lin Ostrom, who went on to become the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Economics, someone may have written something demeaning about my education. “Kila is a smart and good man. I cannot guarantee he has not made mistakes but to suggest he has not gone to school is spectacularly stupid.” (NAN) The post To suggest Anthony Kila hasn’t gone to school is stupid —

item.title: TikTok bans Musk documentary account
item.description: Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk gestures as he speaks during the inaugural parade inside Capitol One Arena, in Washington, DC, on January 20, 2025. (Photo by ANGELA WEISS / AFP) (Photo by ANGELA WEISS/AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Just ahead of the wider release of Alex Gibney's Musk documentary, TikTok has banned the film's social media account from its platform. TikTok did not immediately respond to a request for comment. According to The Hollywood Reporter , the film's distributor, Bleecker Street, was informed Friday afternoon that a "permanent suspension" was imminent. Bleecker Street has not yet responded to a request for comment from The Verge . While TikTok has no official affiliation with Elon Musk, part owner Larry Ellison appears in the film via a text message offering to help Musk fund his Twitter purchase. Last month, YouTube, Meta, X, and TikTok all face … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Unstoppable Barca thrash Betis to extend perfect start
item.description: Hansi Flick’s dominant Barcelona routed 10-man Real Betis 5-2 on Saturday to return five points clear at the top of La Liga. Teenage winger Lamine Yamal scored a brilliant goal for the Spanish champions, with Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric Garcia and Dani Olmo also finding the net at La Cartuja stadium in Seville. Betis, third, had Facundo Bernal sent off for a headbutt on Yamal early in the second half of a pulsating clash. Barca set a new club record for victories at the start of a league campaign and equalled the all-time record of nine, set by Real Madrid in the 1968/69 season. Flick’s side boast 11 wins from 11 games across all competitions. “Once again the team has shown its attacking potential, but it’s also true we’re giving quite a bit away, and that’s probably where the improvement has to come from too,” Rodri told DAZN. Earlier Atletico, second, snatched a late 1-0 win at Espanyol and are five points behind Barca, while Betis are eight points adrift of the leaders and Real Madrid, fourth, host Sevilla on Sunday. Betis rested several players, including key midfielder Isco, ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Feyenoord. Manuel Pellegrini’s side still gave Barca a stern test, after the Catalan giants went ahead through a sensational Yamal strike in the 10th minute. The 19-year-old turned sharply on the edge of the box to escape Bernal and then exquisitely curled into the top corner. “(It was) an incredible goal, we’ve got used to him doing this lately, I have to say,” added Rodri. “In the end, players like that make the difference. But I try to focus on the other things he brings… (like) hard work, a lot of solidarity with the team, understanding the game and where he could find space.” – Defensive flaws – Despite their irresistible attacking play, Barca’s clear weakness under Flick has been their defence and Betis were level before the half-hour mark. A corner came all the way through the box and was recycled by Pablo Fornals, who crossed for Valentin Gomez to head home, getting in front of Barca defender Xavi Espart. Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri put Barca back in front with a header from a corner, before Giovani Lo Celso thought he had equalised in spectacular fashion for the hosts. However the Argentine midfielder’s long-range goal was ruled out for a handball by Cucho Hernandez earlier in the move, much to Betis’ chagrin. Jesus extended Barca’s lead six minutes into the second half from Yamal’s cut-back, moments after having another goal ruled out for offside. Ez Abde immediately pulled one back for Betis during a wild spell, and in the aftermath they were reduced to 10 men when Bernal was sent off for a headbutt on Yamal, who was booked for his part in a confrontation between several players from both sides. Barca added their fourth when Pau Cubarsi nodded the ball across to Garcia to pounce from close range. It was the eighth time this season Flick’s free-scoring side have scored four goals or more in a match.

But I try to focus on the other things he brings… (like) hard work, a lot of solidarity with the team, understanding the game and where he could find space.” – Defensive flaws – Despite their irresistible attacking play, Barca’s clear weakness under Flick has been their defence and Betis were level before the half-hour mark. A corner came all the way through the box and was recycled by Pablo Fornals, who crossed for Valentin Gomez to head home, getting in front of Barca defender Xavi Espart. Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri put Barca back in front with a header from a corner, before Giovani Lo Celso thought he had equalised in spectacular fashion for the hosts. However the Argentine midfielder’s long-range goal was ruled out for a handball by Cucho Hernandez earlier in the move, much to Betis’ chagrin. Jesus extended Barca’s lead six minutes into the second half from Yamal’s cut-back, moments after having another goal ruled out for offside. Ez Abde immediately pulled one back for Betis during a wild spell, and in the aftermath they were reduced to 10 men when Bernal was sent off for a headbutt on Yamal, who was booked for his part in a confrontation between several players from both sides. Barca added their fourth when Pau Cubarsi nodded the ball across to Garcia to pounce from close range. It was the eighth time this season Flick’s free-scoring side have scored four goals or more in a match. The coach brought Raphinha on as a substitute after the Brazilian missed the previous two matches with an injury problem, taking off Yamal to prevent a potential further card and suspension for the Clasico next weekend. First comes the matter of a visit to the French capital on Tuesday to face reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain, which promises to be a thrilling match. Substitute Olmo finished the match off with a neat finish from the edge of the box as Betis backed off to allow Barca’s attention to turn to Europe. Betis defender Hector Bellerin said there were a “couple of unfair decisions” that went against his side but he was pleased with the team’s efforts against his former club. “Facing a team like this, with this quality, we stood up to them until the final minutes,” Bellerin told DAZN. “We showed that with 11 players we’re able to compete against the best.” The post Unstoppable Barca thrash Betis to extend perfect start appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Youth population is Nigeria’s greatest asset – Tinubu
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, OSOGBO President Bola Tinubu has disclosed that Nigeria’s greatest asset is not the mineral deposit beneath its soil but the creative youth population with there resilience and abundant talent. Read Also: Buhari offered to support Osinbajo’s presidential bid four times — Akande counters Babachir Lawal Tinubu said this at the flag off construction of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Centre for Youth Empowerment and Inter-Cultural Dialogue at the Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife Osun State at the weekend. The President was represented by the Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Obafemi Hazmat, said the event transcend a mere celebration but a national statement and deliberate investment in the aspiration of Nigeria’s young population. While describing that the establishment of the centre as timely and strategic, he said the centre offer opportunity to develop a structured platform through which young Nigerians can acquire relevant skills, transform ideas into enterprises, access mentorship. His words, “Today is more than a ceremonial occasion. It is a statement of national purpose. It represents an investment in the aspirations of our young people, a commitment to the unity of our country, and a recognition that Nigeria’s greatest resource is not merely what lies beneath its soil, but the talent, creativity, resilience and enterprise of its people.” “The establishment of this Centre is therefore timely and strategic. It offers an opportunity to develop a structured platform through which young Nigerians can acquire relevant skills, transform ideas into enterprises, access mentorship, engage with industry and international partners, and contribute to national development. He emphasised that the centre’s success should be measured by the opportunities it creates for young people and the lives it transforms. “The true value of this Centre will ultimately be determined not by the magnificence of its buildings, but by the quality of the opportunities it creates and the lives it transforms,” he stated. item.content:encoded: By Shina Abubakar, OSOGBO President Bola Tinubu has disclosed that Nigeria’s greatest asset is not the mineral deposit beneath its soil but the creative youth population with there resilience and abundant talent. Read Also: Buhari offered to support Osinbajo’s presidential bid four times — Akande counters Babachir Lawal Tinubu said this at the flag off construction of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Centre for Youth Empowerment and Inter-Cultural Dialogue at the Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife Osun State at the weekend. The President was represented by the Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Obafemi Hazmat, said the event transcend a mere celebration but a national statement and deliberate investment in the aspiration of Nigeria’s young population. While describing that the establishment of the centre as timely and strategic, he said the centre offer opportunity to develop a structured platform through which young Nigerians can acquire relevant skills, transform ideas into enterprises, access mentorship. His words, “Today is more than a ceremonial occasion. It is a statement of national purpose. It represents an investment in the aspirations of our young people, a commitment to the unity of our country, and a recognition that Nigeria’s greatest resource is not merely what lies beneath its soil, but the talent, creativity, resilience and enterprise of its people.” “The establishment of this Centre is therefore timely and strategic. It offers an opportunity to develop a structured platform through which young Nigerians can acquire relevant skills, transform ideas into enterprises, access mentorship, engage with industry and international partners, and contribute to national development. He emphasised that the centre’s success should be measured by the opportunities it creates for young people and the lives it transforms. “The true value of this Centre will ultimately be determined not by the magnificence of its buildings, but by the quality of the opportunities it creates and the lives it transforms,” he stated. He also called for partnerships among universities, industries, government, investors and international development institutions to connect young people with economic opportunities and help transform their ideas into viable enterprises. He also highlighted the importance of mutual respect and understanding among people from different ethnic, religious and cultural backgrounds, with the aim of promoting national unity, peaceful coexistence and social cohesion. “Our expectation should be that, in the years ahead, this institution will be known not merely as a centre of learning, but as a centre of transformation—one that produces capable leaders, responsible citizens, innovative entrepreneurs and globally competitive professionals. “The Centre should provide a meeting point for universities, industry, government, investors, civil society and international development institutions,” the President said. In his welcome address, the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Simeon Bamire said the centre was conceived as a response to challenges confronting young people, including unemployment, limited access to skills development, unequal economic opportunities and social exclusion. He said the initiative would provide a sustainable platform for equipping young people with practical competencies, promoting enterprise and innovation, and connecting talent with meaningful opportunities. According to him, the centre would serve as an internationally recognised platform where young people from Nigeria, Africa and other parts of the world could learn, collaborate, innovate and develop solutions to shared challenges. “Its programmes would promote entrepreneurship, digital technology, leadership, creative enterprise and peacebuilding, while encouraging cooperation across cultural and national boundaries”, he added. The proposed centre will feature an international conference and dialogue complex, a digital innovation and learning duplex, an entrepreneurship and incubation hub, a scholars and creators lodge, a culture exhibition and community engagement centre, as well as administrative, research and support infrastructure. The project is expected to promote human capital development, employment and enterprise growth, peace, inclusion and social cohesion. It is also intended to provide networking opportunities and support research and policy development. The project is expected to provide young people with opportunities to learn, collaborate, innovate and engage across cultural boundaries. January was mentioned as a target for commissioning the building, although the year was not specified in the information obtained. item.title: 2027: Northern govs pledge total support for Tinubu
item.description: …As Shekarau promises to hit ground running By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja ABUJA: Governors of the northern states have pledged 100 per cent support for President Bola Tinubu, insisting that the North must respect the 1999 understanding between the region and the South on power sharing. Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, spoke on behalf of all the Northern State Governors at the commissioning of the Arewa for Asiwaju A4A national secretariat in Abuja, performed by Vice President Kashim Shettima. “Everywhere, we support the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 100 per cent,” he said. Recalling the agreement, Sani said: “In 1999, there was a mutual agreement between the North and the South that the North would be allowed to go for two consecutive terms in office, and based on that, in the last dispensation, President Buhari, of blessed memory, served for two consecutive terms, meaning for eight years.” He said the South had “every opportunity to present a candidate or candidates,” but did not, because of that agreement and “especially with the support of the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed Tinubu.” Yusuf admitted the arrangement has no constitutional backing, but said that should not matter. “We don’t have any cause to now renege on that promise, even though it is not constitutional. But I can say the constitution of common sense. Common sense dictates that we have to respect this mutual agreement,” he said. The governor told the President that the northern states, “all democrats” and “all patriotic Northern states” were behind him. “He has done exceedingly well, as enumerated by our national chairman,” Sani said. He urged supporters to declare their position publicly. “Don’t be afraid, afraid of facts. We have all agreed we are members of the APC, and therefore, we must work together to ensure that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his Vice President emerge victorious come January 16, by the grace of Allah,” he said. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Tim Burton's 77-Minute Stop-Motion Masterpiece Is Officially Back on Streaming
item.description: When it comes to beautiful, high-quality stop-motion animation, independent studio Laika is the first name that comes to mind. The studio’s hand-crafted puppetry and 3D-printing technology have brought beautiful tales to life for years, from Coraline to ParaNorman . Each has leaned toward more adult themes with gothic narrative undertones, while still focusing heavily on family dynamics. The same is true of Laika’s most recent outing, Travis Knight’s ethereal fantasy film Wildwood .
